sentences.zh: 志第二十九食貨下

translations.literal: Treatise Twenty-Nine: Food and Commerce (Part Two)
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 29: Food and Commerce (Lower Part)

sentences.zh: 武德八年十二月，水部郎中姜行本請於隴州開五節堰，引水通運，許之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighth year of Wude, the Director of the Waterways Bureau, Jiang Xingben, requested opening the Five-Joint Weir at Long Prefecture to divert water for transport; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Wude year 8 (625), Jiang Xingben of the Waterways Bureau petitioned to open the Five-Joint Weir in Long Prefecture and channel water for shipping; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，薛大鼎為滄州刺史，界內有無棣河，隋末填廢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, Xue Dading was Prefect of Cang Prefecture. Within his jurisdiction was the Wudi River, which since the end of Sui had been filled in and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui year 1 (650), Xue Dading became prefect of Cang. His territory included the Wudi River, silted shut since late Sui.

sentences.zh: 大鼎奏開之，引魚鹽於海。

translations.literal: Dading memorialized to open it, drawing fish and salt from the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Dading memorialized to reopen it, drawing seafood and salt inland from the coast.

sentences.zh: 百姓歌之曰：「新河得通舟楫利，直達滄海魚鹽至。

translations.literal: The common people sang in praise, saying: "The new river lets boats pass with ease; straight to the sea the fish and salt come."
translations.idiomatic: The people sang in praise: "The new river lets boats pass with ease; straight to the sea the fish and salt come."

sentences.zh: 昔日徒行今騁駟，美哉薛公德滂被！

translations.literal: "Where once one walked on foot, now one drives a team of four; how fine is Lord Xue's virtue, spreading wide like the flood!"
translations.idiomatic: "Where once we walked, now we ride four-in-hand—how fine is Lord Xue's virtue, spreading wide as the flood!"

sentences.zh: 」咸亨三年，關中饑，監察御史王師順奏請運晉、絳州倉粟以贍之。

translations.literal: " In the third year of Xianheng, Guanzhong suffered famine. Supervising Censor Wang Shishun memorialized requesting transport of grain from the granaries of Jin and Jiang Prefectures to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: " In Xianheng year 3 (672), Guanzhong suffered famine. Supervising censor Wang Shishun petitioned to ship grain from the Jin and Jiang prefectural granaries for relief.

sentences.zh: 上委以運職。

translations.literal: The emperor entrusted him with transport duties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put him in charge of transport.

sentences.zh: 河、渭之間，舟楫相繼，會于渭南，自師順始之也。

translations.literal: Between the Yellow and Wei Rivers, boats followed one after another and assembled at Weinan—this began with Shishun.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yellow and Wei rivers, boats followed one another and gathered at Weinan—Shishun was the first to do this.

sentences.zh: 大足元年六月，於東都立德坊南穿新潭，安置諸州租船。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Dazu, south of Lide Ward in the Eastern Capital they excavated the New Pool to berth tribute ships from the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Dazu year 1 (701), south of Lide Ward in the eastern capital they dug the New Pool to berth tribute ships from the provinces.

sentences.zh: 神龍三年，滄州刺史姜師度於薊州之北，漲水為溝，以備奚、契丹之寇。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenlong, Cang Prefect Jiang Shidu north of Ji Prefecture raised water to form a ditch as a defense against raids by the Xi and Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong year 3 (707), Cang prefect Jiang Shidu north of Ji raised water into a ditch to guard against Xi and Khitan raids.

sentences.zh: 又約舊渠，傍海穿漕，號為平虜渠，以避海難運糧。

translations.literal: He also connected old canals, cutting a transport channel along the coast called the Pacify-the-Barbarians Canal, to avoid shipping grain by sea through hardship.
translations.idiomatic: He also tied in old canals and cut a coastal transport channel called the Pacify-the-Barbarians Canal, so grain could be moved without the perils of open-sea shipping.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，河南尹李傑奏，汴州東有梁公堰，年久堰破，江淮曹運不通。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, Henan Intendant Li Jie memorialized that east of Bian Prefecture was the Duke of Liang Weir, which after many years had broken, so transport from the Jiang-Huai region via the Cao Canal was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan year 2 (714), Henan intendant Li Jie reported that east of Bian stood the Duke of Liang Weir, long broken, blocking Jiang-Huai grain transport on the Cao Canal.

sentences.zh: 發汴、鄭丁夫以浚之。

translations.literal: Corvée laborers from Bian and Zheng were mobilized to dredge it.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée workers from Bian and Zheng were sent to dredge it.

sentences.zh: 省功速就，公私深以為利。

translations.literal: Labor was economized and the work quickly finished; public and private interests alike found it greatly beneficial.
translations.idiomatic: Labor was saved and the work finished quickly; both government and populace profited greatly.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，令將作大匠范安及檢行鄭州河口斗門。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, the Master Builder Fan Anji was ordered to inspect the sluice gates at the Zhengzhou river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 15 (727), master builder Fan Anji was ordered to inspect the sluice gates at the Zhengzhou river mouth.

sentences.zh: 先是，洛陽人劉宗器上言，請塞汜水舊汴河口，於下流滎澤界開梁公堰，置斗門，以通淮、汴，擢拜左衛率府胄曹。

translations.literal: Earlier, a man of Luoyang named Liu Zongqi had submitted a proposal to block the old Bian River mouth at Sishui and open the Duke of Liang Weir at the Xingze boundary downstream, installing sluice gates to connect the Huai and Bian; he was promoted to Registrar of the Left Guard Command.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Zongqi of Luoyang had proposed blocking the old Bian mouth at Sishui and opening the Duke of Liang Weir downstream at the Xingze boundary, with sluice gates to link the Huai and Bian; he was promoted to registrar of the Left Guard Command.

sentences.zh: 至是，新漕塞，行舟不通，貶宗器焉。

translations.literal: At this time the new canal was blocked and boats could not pass; Zongqi was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: By then the new canal was blocked and shipping halted; Zongqi was demoted.

sentences.zh: 安及遂發河南府、懷、鄭、汴、滑三萬人疏決開舊河口，旬日而畢。

translations.literal: Anji then mobilized thirty thousand men from Henan Circuit, Huai, Zheng, Bian, and Hua to dredge and reopen the old river mouth; within ten days it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Anji then mobilized thirty thousand men from Henan, Huai, Zheng, Bian, and Hua to dredge and reopen the old river mouth; within ten days the work was done.

sentences.zh: 十八年，宣州刺史裴耀卿上便宜事條曰：「江南戶口稍廣，倉庫所資，惟出租庸，更無征防。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Xu Prefect Pei Yaojing submitted a list of expedient measures, saying: "The population of Jiangnan has grown somewhat; what supplies the granaries is only the zu-yong tax, with no military levies."
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 (730), Xu prefect Pei Yaojing submitted a list of practical reforms, saying: "Jiangnan's population has grown, yet the granaries are fed only by the zu-yong tax, with no military levies."

sentences.zh: 緣水陸遙遠，轉運艱辛，功力雖勞，倉儲不益。

translations.literal: Because water and land routes are remote, transport is arduous; though labor is expended, storehouses do not increase.
translations.idiomatic: Water and land routes are long, transport arduous; labor is spent, yet the storehouses do not grow.

sentences.zh: 竊見每州所送租及庸調等，本州正二月上道，至揚州入斗門，即逢水淺，已有阻礙，須留一月已上。

translations.literal: I observe that the rent and yong-diao tribute each prefecture sends departs in the first or second month; upon reaching Yangzhou and entering the sluice gates, shallow water already causes obstruction, requiring a stay of more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that rent and yong-diao tribute from each prefecture leave in the first or second month; at Yangzhou's sluice gates shallow water already blocks them, requiring a stay of more than a month.

sentences.zh: 至四月已後，始渡淮入汴，多屬汴河干淺，又般運停留，至六七月始至河口。

translations.literal: Only after the fourth month do they cross the Huai and enter the Bian Canal; mostly the Bian River runs dry and shallow, with transshipment delays, reaching the river mouth only in the sixth or seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the fourth month do they cross the Huai and enter the Bian; the Bian often runs low, transshipment delays pile up, and they reach the river mouth only in the sixth or seventh month.

sentences.zh: 即逢黃河水漲，不得入河。

translations.literal: Then they meet the Yellow River in flood and cannot enter it.
translations.idiomatic: Then they meet the Yellow River in flood and cannot enter it.

sentences.zh: 又須停一兩月，待河水小，始得上河。

translations.literal: They must again wait one or two months until the river subsides before they can ascend it.
translations.idiomatic: They must wait another month or two until the river falls before they can ascend.

sentences.zh: 入洛即漕路幹淺，船艘隘鬧，般載停滯，備極艱辛。

translations.literal: Upon entering Luoyang the canal route is dry and shallow; vessels crowd and jostle, transshipment stalls, and hardship reaches its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang the canal runs dry and shallow; vessels crowd and jam, transshipment stalls, and hardship is extreme.

sentences.zh: 計從江南至東都，停滯日多，得行日少，糧食既皆不足，欠折因此而生。

translations.literal: Calculating from Jiangnan to the Eastern Capital, days of delay are many and days of travel few; grain is insufficient throughout, and shortfalls therefore arise.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiangnan to the eastern capital, delay days outnumber travel days; grain runs short throughout, and shortfalls follow.

sentences.zh: 又江南百姓不習河水，皆轉雇河師水手，更為損費。

translations.literal: Moreover, Jiangnan commoners are unskilled on river water and all hire river pilots and boatmen, which adds further expense.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Jiangnan people are unused to river work and must hire pilots and boatmen, adding further cost.

sentences.zh: 伏見國家舊法，往代成規，擇制便宜，以垂長久。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that the state's old methods and past dynasties' established rules chose what was expedient to endure for long ages.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that the state's old methods and past dynasties' rules chose what was expedient to endure.

sentences.zh: 河口元置武牢倉，江南船不入黃河，即於倉內便貯。

translations.literal: At the river mouth Wulao Granary was originally established; Jiangnan ships did not enter the Yellow River but stored grain conveniently within the granary.
translations.idiomatic: At the river mouth stood Wulao Granary; Jiangnan ships did not enter the Yellow River but stored grain there at once.

sentences.zh: 鞏縣置洛口倉，從黃河不入漕洛，即於倉內安置。

translations.literal: Gong County had Luokou Granary; from the Yellow River grain did not enter the Luoyang canal but was placed within the granary.
translations.idiomatic: Gong County had Luokou Granary; grain from the Yellow River did not enter the Luoyang canal but was stored there.

sentences.zh: 爰及河陽倉、柏崖倉、太原倉、永豐倉、渭南倉，節級取便，例皆如此。

translations.literal: Extending to Heyang, Boya, Taiyuan, Yongfeng, and Weinan granaries—taking convenience at each stage—the precedent was everywhere thus.
translations.idiomatic: The same held for Heyang, Boya, Taiyuan, Yongfeng, and Weinan granaries—convenience at each stage, the rule everywhere alike.

sentences.zh: 水通則隨近運轉，不通即且納在倉，不滯遠船，不憂久耗，比於曠年長運，利便一倍有餘。

translations.literal: When water was open, transport shifted nearby; when blocked, grain was stored in granaries for the time being—distant ships were not detained, long spoilage was not feared; compared with years of extended transport, benefit was more than double.
translations.idiomatic: When water was open, grain moved on nearby; when blocked, it was stored for the moment—distant ships were not held, spoilage was not feared; compared with years of long hauls, the gain was more than double.

sentences.zh: 今若且置武牢、洛口等倉，江南船至河口，即卻還本州，更得其船充運。

translations.literal: Now if Wulao, Luokou, and other granaries are provisionally restored, when Jiangnan ships reach the river mouth they return at once to their home prefecture, and their vessels can be used again for transport.
translations.idiomatic: If Wulao, Luokou, and other granaries are restored now, Jiangnan ships reaching the river mouth would return home at once, freeing those vessels for further transport.

sentences.zh: 並取所減腳錢，更運江淮變造義倉，每年剩得一二百萬石。

translations.literal: Taking together the porterage fees saved, one could further transport Jiang-Huai grain to convert and fill the charity granaries, gaining each year one or two million shi in surplus.
translations.idiomatic: With the porterage fees saved, one could ship Jiang-Huai grain to fill the charity granaries, gaining one or two million shi a year.

sentences.zh: 即望數年之外，倉廩轉加。

translations.literal: Within several years one could expect the granaries to increase further.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the granaries would grow further still.

sentences.zh: 其江淮義倉，下濕不堪久貯，若無船可運，三兩年色變，即給貸費散，公私無益。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Huai charity granaries lie low and damp and cannot store long; without ships to transport, in two or three years the grain spoils and is lent out or dispersed at cost—of no benefit to public or private interests.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai charity granaries are low and damp and cannot store long; without shipping, grain spoils in two or three years and is lent or dispersed at cost—no benefit to state or people.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏不省。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 至二十一年，耀卿為京兆尹，京師雨水害稼，穀價踴貴，玄宗以問耀卿，奏稱：「昔貞觀、永徽之際，祿廩未廣，每歲轉運，不過二十萬石便足。

translations.literal: By the twenty-first year, Yaojing was Intendant of Jingzhao. Rain in the capital region harmed the crops and grain prices soared. Xuanzong questioned Yaojing, who memorialized: "In the Zhenguan and Yonghui era, salary granaries were not extensive; annual transport of no more than two hundred thousand shi sufficed."
translations.idiomatic: By year 21 (733), Yaojing was Jingzhao intendant. Rain in the capital harmed the crops and grain prices soared. Xuanzong asked Yaojing, who replied: "In the Zhenguan and Yonghui era, salary granaries were modest; two hundred thousand shi a year sufficed."

sentences.zh: 今國用漸廣，漕運數倍，猶不能支。

translations.literal: Now state expenditure has gradually expanded; canal transport is several times greater, yet still cannot meet needs.
translations.idiomatic: Now state needs have grown; canal transport is several times greater, yet still cannot keep up.

sentences.zh: 從都至陝，河路艱險，既用陸運，無由廣致。

translations.literal: From the capital to Shan, the river route is perilous; land transport is used instead, so there is no way to bring in more.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital to Shan the river route is perilous; land transport is used instead, so supply cannot be expanded.

sentences.zh: 若能兼河漕，變陸為水，則所支有餘，動盈萬計。

translations.literal: If river transport can be added and land carriage changed to water, expenditures would have surplus, often by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: If river transport can be added and land carriage turned to water, supply would exceed need by tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 且江南租船，候水始進，吳人不便漕挽，由是所在停留。

translations.literal: Moreover, Jiangnan tribute ships wait for water before advancing; Wu people are unaccustomed to canal towing, and therefore halt everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Jiangnan tribute ships wait for water before advancing; Wu people are unused to canal towing and halt everywhere.

sentences.zh: 日月既淹，遂生竊盜。

translations.literal: As days and months drag on, theft arises.
translations.idiomatic: As time drags on, theft follows.

sentences.zh: 臣望於河口置一倉，納江東租米，便放船歸。

translations.literal: Your subject proposes establishing a granary at the river mouth to receive Jiangdong tribute rice and release the ships to return at once.
translations.idiomatic: I propose a granary at the river mouth to receive Jiangdong tribute rice and release the ships to return at once.

sentences.zh: 從河口即分入河、洛，官自雇船載運。

translations.literal: From the river mouth it would be divided into the Yellow River and Luoyang routes; the government would hire boats to carry it.
translations.idiomatic: From the river mouth it would be split between the Yellow River and Luoyang routes, with the government hiring boats to carry it.

sentences.zh: 三門之東，置一倉。

translations.literal: East of Sanmen, establish a granary.
translations.idiomatic: East of Sanmen, establish a granary.

sentences.zh: 三門既水險，即於河岸開山，車運十數里。

translations.literal: Sanmen being perilous in water, cut through the mountain at the riverbank and transport by cart for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Sanmen being perilous, cut through the bank and cart grain more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 三門之西，又置一倉，每運至倉，即般下貯納。

translations.literal: West of Sanmen, establish another granary; whenever transport reaches a granary, unload and store it.
translations.idiomatic: West of Sanmen, establish another granary; whenever a shipment reaches a granary, unload and store it.

sentences.zh: 水通即運，水細便止。

translations.literal: When water is open, transport; when low, halt.
translations.idiomatic: When water is open, ship; when low, halt.

sentences.zh: 自太原倉溯河，更無停留，所省钜萬。

translations.literal: From Taiyuan Granary upstream on the river there would be no further delay; savings would amount to vast sums.
translations.idiomatic: From Taiyuan Granary upstream there would be no further delay; savings would run to vast sums.

sentences.zh: 前漢都關中，年月稍久，及隋亦在京師，緣河皆有舊倉，所以國用常贍。

translations.literal: Former Han made its capital in Guanzhong for a long time; Sui also was at the capital. Along the rivers were old granaries everywhere, and therefore state expenditure was always provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han long made its capital in Guanzhong; Sui too was at the capital. Old granaries lined the rivers, and state needs were always met.

sentences.zh: 」上深然其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor strongly approved.

sentences.zh: 至二十二年八月，置河陰縣及河陰倉、河西柏崖倉、三門東集津倉、三門西鹽倉。

translations.literal: By the eighth month of the twenty-second year, Heyin County and Heyin Granary were established, also Hexi Boya Granary, Sanmen East Jijin Granary, and Sanmen West Yan Granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 22 (734), Heyin County and Heyin Granary were established, along with Hexi Boya Granary, Sanmen East Jijin Granary, and Sanmen West Yan Granary.

sentences.zh: 開三門山十八里，以避湍險。

translations.literal: Sanmen Mountain was cut open for eighteen li to avoid rapids and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Sanmen Mountain was cut for eighteen li to avoid the rapids.

sentences.zh: 自江淮而溯鴻溝，悉納河陰倉。

translations.literal: From the Jiang-Huai region upstream along the Hong Canal, all was received into Heyin Granary.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jiang-Huai upstream along the Hong Canal, all grain went into Heyin Granary.

sentences.zh: 自河陰送納含嘉倉，又送納太原倉，謂之北運。

translations.literal: From Heyin it was sent to Hanjia Granary and then to Taiyuan Granary—called the Northern Transport.
translations.idiomatic: From Heyin it was sent to Hanjia Granary and then Taiyuan Granary—the Northern Transport.

sentences.zh: 自太原倉浮於渭，以實關中。

translations.literal: From Taiyuan Granary it was floated on the Wei to fill Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: From Taiyuan Granary it was floated on the Wei to supply Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 上大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 尋以耀卿為黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事，充江淮、河南轉運都使。

translations.literal: Soon Yaojing was made Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Associate Chief Councilor, serving as overall transport commissioner for Jiang-Huai and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yaojing was made vice director of the Palace Secretariat and associate chief councilor, serving as overall transport commissioner for Jiang-Huai and Henan.

sentences.zh: 以鄭州刺史崔希逸、河南少尹蕭炅為副。

translations.literal: Zheng Prefect Cui Xiyi and Henan Vice Intendant Xiao Jiong were made his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng prefect Cui Xiyi and Henan vice intendant Xiao Jiong served as deputies.

sentences.zh: 凡三年，運七百萬石，省陸運之傭四十萬貫。

translations.literal: In all, over three years seven million shi were transported, saving four hundred thousand strings in land-transport porterage.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years seven million shi were transported, saving four hundred thousand strings in land-transport costs.

sentences.zh: 舊制，東都含嘉倉積江淮之米，載以大輿而西，至於陝三百里，率兩斛計傭錢千。

translations.literal: Under the old system, the Eastern Capital's Hanjia Granary stored Jiang-Huai rice, loaded on great carts and hauled west three hundred li to Shan; for every two hu, porterage was reckoned at one thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, the eastern capital's Hanjia Granary stored Jiang-Huai rice, hauled west three hundred li to Shan on great carts; porterage was one thousand cash per two hu.

sentences.zh: 此耀卿所省之數也。

translations.literal: This was the sum Yaojing saved.
translations.idiomatic: This was the sum Yaojing saved.

sentences.zh: 明年，耀卿拜侍中，而蕭炅代焉。

translations.literal: The next year Yaojing was appointed Palace Attendant, and Xiao Jiong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yaojing became palace attendant, and Xiao Jiong replaced him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，運米一百萬石。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, one million shi of rice were transported.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 (737), one million shi of rice were transported.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，陝郡太守李濟物，鑿三門山以通運，辟三門巔，逾岩險之地，俾負索引艦，升于安流，自濟物始也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Shan Prefect Li Jiwu cut through Sanmen Mountain for transport, opening the Sanmen peaks and crossing rocky perilous ground, making bearers haul ships with ropes to raise them into calm current—this began with Jiwu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 (741), Shan prefect Li Jiwu cut Sanmen Mountain for transport, opening the peaks and crossing perilous rock, with bearers hauling ships by rope into calm water—Jiwu was the first to do this.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載，韋堅代蕭炅，以滻水作廣運潭于望春樓之東，而藏舟焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, Wei Jian replaced Xiao Jiong, using Chan River water to make the Broad Transport Pool east of Wangchun Tower to berth ships.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 3 (744), Wei Jian replaced Xiao Jiong, diverting Chan River water to create the Broad Transport Pool east of Wangchun Tower to berth ships.

sentences.zh: 是年，楊釗以殿中侍御史為水陸運使，以代韋堅。

translations.literal: That year Yang Zhao was made Palace Censor as Commissioner of Water and Land Transport to replace Wei Jian.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yang Zhao was made palace censor as commissioner of water and land transport to replace Wei Jian.

sentences.zh: 先是，米至京師，或砂礫糠紕，雜乎其間。

translations.literal: Earlier, when rice reached the capital, sand, gravel, chaff, and bran were sometimes mixed in.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when rice reached the capital, sand, gravel, chaff, and bran were sometimes mixed in.

sentences.zh: 開元初，詔使揚擲而較其虛實，「揚擲」之名，自此始也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan an edict ordered tossing and winnowing to compare actual and nominal amounts—the name "toss and winnow" dates from this.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiyuan an edict ordered tossing and winnowing to check actual against nominal amounts—the term "toss and winnow" dates from then.

sentences.zh: 十四載八月，詔水陸運宜停一年。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year, an edict ordered water and land transport to halt for one year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 14 (755), an edict ordered water and land transport halted for one year.

sentences.zh: 天寶以來，楊國忠、王鉷皆兼重使以權天下。

translations.literal: Since Tianbao, Yang Guozhong and Wang Hong each held multiple heavy commissions to wield power over the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tianbao, Yang Guozhong and Wang Hong each held multiple heavy commissions to wield power over the realm.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，第五琦始以錢穀得見。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign, Diwu Qi first gained audience through fiscal grain affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign, Diwu Qi first gained audience through fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 請于江、淮分置租庸使，市輕貨以救軍食，遂拜監察御史，為之使。

translations.literal: He requested establishing zu-yong commissioners separately in the Jiang and Huai regions to purchase light goods to relieve army provisions; he was then appointed Supervising Censor and made commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to establish zu-yong commissioners in the Jiang and Huai regions to buy light goods for army provisions; he was appointed supervising censor and made commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，加度支郎中，尋兼中丞，為鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan he was added as Director of the Revenue Bureau; soon he also held Vice Censor-in-Chief and became Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan year 1 (758) he was made director of the Revenue Bureau; soon he also held vice censor-in-chief and became salt and iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 於是始大鹽法，就山海井灶，收榷其鹽，立監院官吏。

translations.literal: Thereupon the great salt monopoly began: at mountain, sea, and well saltworks, salt was collected under state monopoly, and supervisory offices and officials were established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the great salt monopoly began: at mountain, sea, and well saltworks salt was monopolized, with supervisory offices and officials established.

sentences.zh: 其舊業戶洎浮人欲以鹽為業者，免其雜役，隸鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: Former producers and floating persons wishing to take salt as their trade were exempted from miscellaneous corvée and placed under the Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Former producers and itinerants wishing to work in salt were exempted from miscellaneous corvée and placed under the salt and iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 常戶自租庸外無橫賦。

translations.literal: Regular households beyond zu-yong had no additional levies.
translations.idiomatic: Regular households beyond zu-yong faced no extra levies.

sentences.zh: 人不益稅，而國用以饒。

translations.literal: The people were not increased in tax, yet state expenditure was ample.
translations.idiomatic: The people were not taxed more, yet state revenue was ample.

sentences.zh: 明年，琦以戶部侍郎同平章事，詔兵部侍郎呂諲代之。

translations.literal: The next year Qi was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Associate Chief Councilor; an edict had Vice Minister of War Lü Yin replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Qi became vice minister of revenue and associate chief councilor; vice minister of war Lü Yin was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年五月，元載以中書侍郎代呂諲。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Baoying, Yuan Zai as Vice Director of the Secretariat replaced Lü Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Baoying year 1 (762), Yuan Zai as vice director of the Secretariat replaced Lü Yin.

sentences.zh: 是時淮、河阻兵，飛挽路絕，鹽鐵租賦，皆溯漢而上。

translations.literal: At this time the Huai and Yellow River routes were blocked by warfare; rapid transport routes were cut off; salt, iron, rent, and levies all went upstream on the Han.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Huai and Yellow routes were blocked by war; rapid transport was cut off; salt, iron, rent, and levies all went upstream on the Han.

sentences.zh: 以侍御史穆甯為河南道轉運租庸鹽鐵使，尋加戶部員外，遷鄂州刺史，以總東南貢賦。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Mu Ning was made Henan Circuit Transport, Zu-Yong, and Salt and Iron Commissioner; soon he was added as Revenue Bureau Vice Director, transferred to Prefect of E, to oversee southeastern tribute and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant censor Mu Ning was made Henan transport, zu-yong, and salt and iron commissioner; soon he was added revenue bureau vice director and transferred to E prefect to oversee southeastern tribute.

sentences.zh: 是時朝議以寇盜未戢，關東漕運，宜有倚辦，遂以通州刺史劉晏為戶部侍郎、京兆尹、度支鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: At this time court discussion held that since bandits were not yet pacified, Guandong canal transport needed a reliable manager; thus Tong Prefect Liu Yan was made Vice Minister of Revenue, Intendant of Jingzhao, and Revenue, Salt, Iron, and Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion held that with bandits not yet pacified, Guandong canal transport needed a reliable manager; Tong prefect Liu Yan was made vice minister of revenue, Jingzhao intendant, and revenue, salt, iron, and transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵兼漕運，自晏始也。

translations.literal: Combining salt and iron with canal transport began with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Combining salt and iron with canal transport began with Yan.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜吏部尚書、同平章事，依前充使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Minister of Personnel and Associate Chief Councilor, continuing as before as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was appointed minister of personnel and associate chief councilor, continuing as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晏始以鹽利為漕傭，自江淮至渭橋，率十萬斛傭七千緡，補綱吏督之。

translations.literal: Yan first used salt profits for canal porterage; from Jiang-Huai to Weiqiao, for every hundred thousand hu, seven thousand strings in porterage, supplemented by net officers to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Yan first used salt profits for canal porterage; from Jiang-Huai to Weiqiao, seven thousand strings per hundred thousand hu, with net officers to supervise.

sentences.zh: 不發丁男，不勞郡縣，蓋自古未之有也。

translations.literal: Corvée men were not mobilized and prefectures and counties were not burdened—such a thing had never been since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée men were not mobilized and prefectures and counties were not burdened—unprecedented since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自此歲運米數千萬石，自淮北列置巡院，搜擇能吏以主之，廣牢盆以來商賈。

translations.literal: From this time tens of millions of shi of rice were transported yearly; south of the Huai inspection posts were set in series, capable officials selected to manage them, and salt pans expanded to attract merchants.
translations.idiomatic: From then tens of millions of shi of rice were shipped yearly; south of the Huai inspection posts were set in series, capable officials chosen to run them, and salt pans expanded to attract merchants.

sentences.zh: 凡所制置，皆自晏始。

translations.literal: All institutions established were begun by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: All these institutions began with Yan.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年正月，復以第五琦專判度支鑄錢鹽鐵事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Guangde, Diwu Qi was again put solely in charge of revenue, coinage, and salt and iron affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Guangde year 2 (764), Diwu Qi was again put solely in charge of revenue, coinage, and salt and iron.

sentences.zh: 而晏以檢校戶部尚書為河南及江淮已來轉運使，及與河南副元帥計會開決汴河。

translations.literal: Yan as Acting Minister of Revenue was Transport Commissioner for Henan and all regions from Jiang-Huai eastward, and together with the Henan deputy supreme commander planned to open and dredge the Bian Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Yan as acting minister of revenue was transport commissioner for Henan and all regions from Jiang-Huai eastward, and with the Henan deputy supreme commander planned to open and dredge the Bian Canal.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，晏為東道轉運常平鑄錢鹽鐵使，琦為關內、河東，劍南三川轉運常平鑄錢鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai, Yan was Eastern Circuit Transport, Ever-Normal, Coinage, and Salt and Iron Commissioner; Qi was Guannei, Hedong, and Jiannan Three Rivers Transport, Ever-Normal, Coinage, and Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai year 2 (766), Yan was eastern circuit transport, ever-normal, coinage, and salt and iron commissioner; Qi was Guannei, Hedong, and Jiannan Three Rivers transport, ever-normal, coinage, and salt and iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大曆五年，詔停關內、河東、三川轉運常平鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dali, an edict halted the Guannei, Hedong, and Three Rivers transport, ever-normal, and salt and iron commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali year 5 (770), an edict halted the Guannei, Hedong, and Three Rivers transport, ever-normal, and salt and iron commissioners.

sentences.zh: 自此晏與戶部侍郎韓滉分領關內、河東、山、劍租庸青苗使。

translations.literal: From this Yan and Vice Minister of Revenue Han Huang divided leadership of Guannei, Hedong, Shan, and Jian zu-yong and green-sprout commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: From then Yan and vice minister of revenue Han Huang divided leadership of Guannei, Hedong, Shan, and Jian zu-yong and green-sprout commissioners.

sentences.zh: 至十四年，天下財賦，皆以晏掌之。

translations.literal: By the fourteenth year, all revenue and levies under Heaven were managed by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: By year 14 (779), all revenue under heaven was managed by Yan.

sentences.zh: 建中初，宰相楊炎用事，尤惡劉晏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Chief Councilor Yang Yan held power and especially hated Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong (780), chief councilor Yang Yan held power and especially hated Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 炎乃奪其權。

translations.literal: Yan then stripped him of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then stripped him of authority.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕以徵稅多門，郡邑凋耗，聽於群議，思有變更，將致時雍，宜遵古制。

translations.literal: An edict said: "We find levies in many channels and prefectures and districts depleted. Heeding collective counsel, We seek change to bring timely harmony and should follow the ancient system."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "We find levies in many channels and prefectures depleted. Heeding counsel, We seek change to bring harmony and should follow the ancient system."

sentences.zh: 其江淮米准旨轉運入京者，及諸軍糧儲，宜令庫部郎中崔河圖權領之。

translations.literal: Jiang-Huai rice transported to the capital by imperial order, and grain stores for the various armies, should be placed under acting management of Treasury Bureau Director Cui Hetu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai rice shipped to the capital by imperial order and grain stores for the armies should be placed under acting management of treasury bureau director Cui Hetu.

sentences.zh: 今年夏稅以前，諸道財賦多輸京者，及鹽鐵財貨，委江州刺史包佶權領之。

translations.literal: Before this year's summer tax, revenues from the circuits mostly sent to the capital, and salt and iron goods, were entrusted to acting management by Jiang Prefect Bao Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Before this year's summer tax, circuit revenues mostly sent to the capital and salt and iron goods were entrusted to acting management by Jiang prefect Bao Ji.

sentences.zh: 天下錢穀，皆歸金部、倉部。

translations.literal: All money and grain under Heaven were returned to the Gold Bureau and Granary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: All money and grain under heaven returned to the Gold Bureau and Granary Bureau.

sentences.zh: 委中書門下簡兩司郎官，准格式條理。

translations.literal: The Secretariat-Chancellery was entrusted to select bureau directors from the two bureaus to administer according to regulations and forms.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat-chancellery was entrusted to select bureau directors from the two bureaus to administer according to regulations.

sentences.zh: 」尋貶晏為忠州刺史。

translations.literal: " Soon Yan was demoted to Prefect of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Yan was demoted to prefect of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 晏既罷黜，天下錢穀歸尚書省。

translations.literal: Once Yan was dismissed, all money and grain under Heaven returned to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan was dismissed, all money and grain returned to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 既而出納無所統，乃復置使領之。

translations.literal: But then receipts and disbursements had no overall control, and commissioners were again established to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: But receipts and disbursements lacked overall control, and commissioners were again established.

sentences.zh: 其年三月，以韓洄為戶部侍郎，判度支；

translations.literal: In the third month of that year, Han Tao was made Vice Minister of Revenue and put in charge of the Revenue Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of that year, Han Tao was made vice minister of revenue and put in charge of the Revenue Bureau;

sentences.zh: 金部郎中杜佑權勾當江淮水陸運使。

translations.literal: Gold Bureau Director Du You was put in acting charge of the Jiang-Huai water and land transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gold bureau director Du You was put in acting charge of the Jiang-Huai water and land transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 炎尋殺晏於忠州。

translations.literal: Yang Yan soon had Liu Yan killed at Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan soon had Liu Yan killed at Zhong.

sentences.zh: 自兵興已來，凶荒相屬，京師米斛萬錢，官廚無兼時之食。

translations.literal: Since warfare arose, famine followed in succession; in the capital a hu of rice cost ten thousand cash, and the official kitchens had no food for two meals.
translations.idiomatic: Since warfare arose, famine followed in succession; in the capital a hu of rice cost ten thousand cash, and the official kitchens had no food for two meals.

sentences.zh: 百姓在畿甸者，拔穀挼穗，以供禁軍。

translations.literal: Commoners in the capital region pulled up grain and stripped ears to supply the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners in the capital region pulled up grain and stripped ears to supply the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 洎晏掌國計，復江淮轉運之制，歲入米數十萬斛以濟關中。

translations.literal: When Yan took charge of state accounts, he restored the Jiang-Huai transport system; each year several hundred thousand hu of rice entered to relieve Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan took charge of state accounts, he restored Jiang-Huai transport; each year several hundred thousand hu of rice reached Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 代第五琦領鹽務，其法益密。

translations.literal: Replacing Diwu Qi in charge of salt affairs, his methods grew ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing Diwu Qi in charge of salt affairs, his methods grew ever tighter.

sentences.zh: 初年入錢六十萬，季年則十倍其初。

translations.literal: In the first year cash receipts were six hundred thousand; in the final year they were ten times the first.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year cash receipts were six hundred thousand; in the final year they were ten times that.

sentences.zh: 大曆末，通天下之財，而計其所入，總一千二百萬貫，而鹽利過半。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali, all wealth under Heaven was tallied; total receipts amounted to twelve million strings, of which salt profits exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Dali, all wealth under heaven was tallied; total receipts were twelve million strings, of which salt profits exceeded half.

sentences.zh: 李靈耀之亂，河南皆為盜據，不奉法制，賦稅不上供，州縣益減。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Li Lingyao, Henan was all held by bandits who did not obey law and regulation; taxes and levies were not submitted, and prefectures and counties dwindled further.
translations.idiomatic: In Li Lingyao's rebellion, Henan was held by bandits who ignored law; taxes were not submitted, and prefectures and counties dwindled.

sentences.zh: 晏以羨餘相補，人不加賦，所入仍舊，議者稱之。

translations.literal: Yan used surpluses to make up deficits; the people were not increased in levies, yet receipts remained as before—commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Yan used surpluses to cover deficits; the people were not taxed more, yet receipts held steady—commentators praised this.

sentences.zh: 其相與商榷財用之術者，必一時之選。

translations.literal: Those who discussed fiscal methods with him were invariably the finest men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Those who discussed fiscal methods with him were invariably the finest men of the age.

sentences.zh: 故晏沒後二十年，韓洄、元琇、裴腆、包佶、盧徵、李衡相繼分掌財賦，出晏門下。

translations.literal: Thus for twenty years after Yan's death, Han Tao, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Bao Ji, Lu Zheng, and Li Heng in succession divided management of revenues—all from Yan's school.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years after Yan's death, Han Tao, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Bao Ji, Lu Zheng, and Li Heng in succession divided revenues—all from Yan's school.

sentences.zh: 屬吏在千里外，奉教如目前。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials a thousand li away carried out instructions as if before his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates a thousand li away carried out instructions as if he stood before them.

sentences.zh: 四方水旱，及軍府纖芥，莫不先知焉。

translations.literal: Flood and drought in the four directions, and the slightest matter in army offices—none escaped prior knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Flood and drought everywhere, the slightest matter in army offices—he knew of all beforehand.

sentences.zh: 其年詔曰：「天下山澤之利，當歸王者，宜總榷鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: That year an edict said: "Profits from mountains and marshes under Heaven should belong to the sovereign; there should be an overall salt and iron monopoly commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict said: "Profits from mountains and marshes under heaven belong to the sovereign; there should be an overall salt and iron monopoly commissioner."

sentences.zh: 三年，以包佶為左庶子、汴東水陸運鹽鐵租庸使，崔縱為右庶子、汴西水陸運鹽鐵租庸使。

translations.literal: In the third year, Bao Ji was made Left Vice Heir Apparent and Bian East Water-Land Transport, Salt, Iron, and Zu-Yong Commissioner; Cui Zong was made Right Vice Heir Apparent and Bian West Water-Land Transport, Salt, Iron, and Zu-Yong Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, Bao Ji was made left vice heir apparent and Bian east water-land transport, salt, iron, and zu-yong commissioner; Cui Zong was made right vice heir apparent and Bian west commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，度支侍郎趙贊議常平事，竹、木、茶、漆盡稅之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan proposed ever-normal granary affairs; bamboo, wood, tea, and lacquer were all taxed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, revenue vice minister Zhao Zan proposed ever-normal granary affairs; bamboo, wood, tea, and lacquer were all taxed.

sentences.zh: 茶之有稅，肇於此矣。

translations.literal: Taxation on tea began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Taxation on tea began here.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，元琇以御史大夫為鹽鐵水陸運使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, Yuan Xiu as Censor-in-Chief was made Salt, Iron, and Water-Land Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 1 (785), Yuan Xiu as censor-in-chief was made salt, iron, and water-land transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，以尚書右僕射韓滉統之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Han Huang was put in overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year, right vice director Han Huang was put in overall charge.

sentences.zh: 滉歿，宰相竇參代之。

translations.literal: When Huang died, Chief Councilor Dou Can replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang died, chief councilor Dou Can replaced him.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，度支轉運鹽鐵奏：「比年自揚子運米，皆分配緣路觀察使差長綱發遣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year, the Revenue, Transport, and Salt and Iron offices memorialized: "In recent years rice transported from Yangzi has all been assigned to circuit observation commissioners along the route to dispatch chief convoy leaders."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 5, revenue, transport, and salt and iron offices memorialized: "In recent years rice from Yangzi has been assigned to circuit observation commissioners along the route to dispatch convoy leaders."

sentences.zh: 運路既遠，實謂勞人。

translations.literal: The transport route being remote, this truly burdens the people.
translations.idiomatic: The route being remote, this truly burdens the people.

sentences.zh: 今請當使諸院，自差綱節級般運，以救邊食。

translations.literal: We now request that the commissioner's various posts themselves dispatch convoy leaders in stages for transshipment to relieve frontier provisions.
translations.idiomatic: We now request the commissioner's posts themselves dispatch convoy leaders in stages to relieve frontier provisions.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔：東南兩稅財賦，自河南、江淮、嶺南、山南東道至於渭橋，以戶部侍郎張滂主之；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict: Southeastern two-tax revenues from Henan, Jiang-Huai, Lingnan, and Shannan East Circuit to Weiqiao were to be overseen by Vice Minister of Revenue Zhang Pang;
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, an edict: southeastern two-tax revenues from Henan, Jiang-Huai, Lingnan, and Shannan east to Weiqiao were overseen by revenue vice minister Zhang Pang;

sentences.zh: 河東、劍南、山南西道，以戶部尚書度支使班宏主之。

translations.literal: Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan West Circuit were to be overseen by Minister of Revenue and Revenue Commissioner Ban Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan west were overseen by revenue minister and revenue commissioner Ban Hong.

sentences.zh: 今戶部所領三川鹽鐵轉運，自此始也。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue's leadership of Three Rivers salt, iron, and transport began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue's leadership of Three Rivers salt, iron, and transport began here.

sentences.zh: 其後宏、滂互有短長。

translations.literal: Thereafter Hong and Pang each had strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Hong and Pang each had strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 宰相趙憬、陸贄以其事上聞，由是遵大曆故事，如劉晏、韓滉所分焉。

translations.literal: Chief Councilors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi reported the matter to the throne; thereby the Dali precedent was followed, as Liu Yan and Han Huang had divided it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councilors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi reported to the throne; thereby the Dali precedent was followed, as Liu Yan and Han Huang had divided it.

sentences.zh: 九年，張滂奏立稅茶法。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Zhang Pang memorialized to establish the tea tax law.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, Zhang Pang memorialized to establish the tea tax law.

sentences.zh: 自後裴延齡專判度支，與鹽鐵益殊塗而理矣。

translations.literal: From then on Pei Yanling solely judged the Revenue Bureau, and salt and iron were increasingly administered by separate paths.
translations.idiomatic: From then Pei Yanling solely ran the Revenue Bureau, and salt and iron were increasingly administered separately.

sentences.zh: 十年，潤州刺史王緯代之，理于硃方。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Run Prefect Wang Wei replaced him, administering from Zhufang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, Run prefect Wang Wei replaced him, administering from Zhufang.

sentences.zh: 數年而李錡代之，鹽院津堰，改張侵剝，不知紀極。

translations.literal: After several years Li Qian replaced him; at salt offices, ferry crossings, and weirs, alterations and extensions of exactions knew no limit.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Li Qian replaced him; at salt offices, ferries, and weirs, exactions multiplied beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 私路小堰，厚斂行人，多自錡始。

translations.literal: Private routes and small weirs heavily taxing travelers largely began with Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy tolls on private routes and small weirs largely began with Qian.

sentences.zh: 時鹽鐵轉運有上都留後，以副使潘孟陽主之。

translations.literal: At the time salt and iron transport had an upper capital rear commissioner, managed by Vice Commissioner Pan Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time salt and iron transport had an upper capital rear commissioner, managed by vice commissioner Pan Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 王叔文權傾朝野，亦以鹽鐵副使兼學士為留後。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen's power dominated court and countryside; he too served as salt and iron vice commissioner and academician as rear commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen's power dominated court and countryside; he too served as salt and iron vice commissioner and academician as rear commissioner.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，有司重奏鹽法，以杜佑判鹽鐵轉運使，理於揚州。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended, the relevant offices again memorialized on the salt law; Du You was put in charge of salt and iron transport commissioner, administering from Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended, the relevant offices again memorialized on the salt law; Du You was put in charge of salt and iron transport, administering from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 元和二年三月，以李巽代之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Yuanhe, Li Xun replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yuanhe year 2 (807), Li Xun replaced him.

sentences.zh: 先是，李錡判使，天下榷酤漕運，由其操割，專事貢獻，牢其寵渥。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Qian was commissioner, monopoly wine and canal transport under Heaven were manipulated by him; he devoted himself to tribute offerings to secure favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Li Qian was commissioner, monopoly wine and canal transport were in his hands; he devoted himself to tribute to secure favor.

sentences.zh: 中朝柄事者悉以利積於私室，而國用日耗。

translations.literal: Those who held power at court all accumulated profit in private chambers, while state expenditure daily dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Court power-holders all accumulated profit privately, while state revenue daily dwindled.

sentences.zh: 巽既為鹽鐵使，大正其事。

translations.literal: Once Xun became salt and iron commissioner, he greatly rectified the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xun became salt and iron commissioner, he greatly rectified affairs.

sentences.zh: 其堰埭先隸浙西觀察使者，悉歸之；

translations.literal: Weirs and dams formerly subordinate to the Zhexi observation commissioner were all returned to him;
translations.idiomatic: Weirs and dams formerly under the Zhexi observation commissioner were all returned to him;

sentences.zh: 因循權置者，盡罷之；

translations.literal: those established by precedent and temporary authority were all abolished;
translations.idiomatic: those established by precedent and temporary authority were all abolished;

sentences.zh: 增置河陰敖倉；

translations.literal: Heyin Ao Granary was added;
translations.idiomatic: Heyin Ao Granary was added;

sentences.zh: 置桂陽監，鑄平陽銅山為錢。

translations.literal: Guiyang Directorate was established to cast coin from Pingyang copper mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang directorate was established to cast coin from Pingyang copper mountain.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「江淮、河南、峽內、兗鄆、嶺南鹽法監院，去年收鹽價緡錢七百二十七萬，比舊法張其估一千七百八十余萬，非實數也。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Salt law supervisory offices in Jiang-Huai, Henan, within the Gorges, Yan-Yun, and Lingnan last year collected salt-price cash of seven million two hundred seventy thousand strings; compared with the old law inflating valuations to more than seventeen million eight hundred thousand—this is not the real figure."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Salt supervisory offices in Jiang-Huai, Henan, the gorges, Yan-Yun, and Lingnan last year collected seven million two hundred seventy thousand strings in salt revenue; compared with the old law's inflated valuation of more than seventeen million eight hundred thousand—not the real figure."

sentences.zh: 今請以其數，除煮之外，付度支收其數。

translations.literal: We now request that this figure, aside from boiling costs, be handed to the Revenue Bureau to collect.
translations.idiomatic: We now request that this figure, aside from boiling costs, be handed to the Revenue Bureau to collect.

sentences.zh: 」鹽鐵使煮鹽利系度支，自此始也。

translations.literal: " The salt and iron commissioner's boiled-salt profits being tied to the Revenue Bureau began from this.
translations.idiomatic: " Tying the salt and iron commissioner's boiled-salt profits to the Revenue Bureau began here.

sentences.zh: 又以程異為揚子留後。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi was also made Yangzi rear commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi was also made Yangzi rear commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四月五日，巽卒。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fourth month, Xun died.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fourth month, Xun died.

sentences.zh: 自榷筦之興，惟劉晏得其術，而巽次之。

translations.literal: Since monopolies arose, only Liu Yan mastered the method, with Xun second.
translations.idiomatic: Since monopolies arose, only Liu Yan mastered the method; Xun was second.

sentences.zh: 然初年之利，類晏之季年；

translations.literal: Yet profits in his first years resembled Yan's final years;
translations.idiomatic: Yet profits in his first years resembled Yan's final years;

sentences.zh: 季年之利，則三倍于晏矣。

translations.literal: profits in his final years were three times Yan's.
translations.idiomatic: profits in his final years were three times Yan's.

sentences.zh: 舊制，每歲運江淮米五十萬斛，至河陰留十萬，四十萬送渭倉。

translations.literal: Under the old system, each year five hundred thousand hu of Jiang-Huai rice were transported; one hundred thousand were left at Heyin, four hundred thousand sent to the Wei granary.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, each year five hundred thousand hu of Jiang-Huai rice were transported; one hundred thousand were left at Heyin, four hundred thousand sent to the Wei granary.

sentences.zh: 晏歿，久不登其數，惟巽秉使三載，無升鬥之闕焉。

translations.literal: After Yan's death the quota was long unmet; only in Xun's three years holding the commission was there no shortfall of a sheng or dou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan's death the quota was long unmet; only in Xun's three years as commissioner was there no shortfall.

sentences.zh: 六月，以河東節度使李鄘代之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Hedong Military Commissioner Li Yun replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Hedong military commissioner Li Yun replaced him.

sentences.zh: 五年，李鄘為淮南節度使，以宣州觀察使盧坦代之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Li Yun became Huainan Military Commissioner; Xu Observation Commissioner Lu Tan replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, Li Yun became Huainan military commissioner; Xu observation commissioner Lu Tan replaced him.

sentences.zh: 六年，坦奏，每年江淮運米四十萬石到渭橋，近日欠闕太半，請旋收糴，遞年貯備。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Tan memorialized that each year four hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice reached Weiqiao, but recently shortfalls exceeded half; he requested immediate grain purchases and year-by-year storage.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, Tan memorialized that each year four hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice reached Weiqiao, but recently shortfalls exceeded half; he requested immediate purchases and year-by-year storage.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 坦改戶部侍郎，以京兆尹王播代之。

translations.literal: Tan was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue; Jingzhao Intendant Wang Bo replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was transferred to revenue vice minister; Jingzhao intendant Wang Bo replaced him.

sentences.zh: 播遂奏：「元和五年，江淮、河南、嶺南、峽中、兗鄆等鹽利錢六百九十八萬貫。

translations.literal: Bo then memorialized: "In the fifth year of Yuanhe, salt profits from Jiang-Huai, Henan, Lingnan, within the Gorges, and Yan-Yun amounted to six million nine hundred eighty thousand strings."
translations.idiomatic: Bo then memorialized: "In Yuanhe year 5, salt profits from Jiang-Huai, Henan, Lingnan, the gorges, and Yan-Yun amounted to six million nine hundred eighty thousand strings."

sentences.zh: 比量改法已前舊鹽利，時價四倍虛估，即此錢為一千七百四十餘萬貫矣，請付度支收管。

translations.literal: Compared with old salt profits before the law was changed, at four times current price in inflated valuation this cash would be more than seventeen million four hundred thousand strings; we request it be handed to the Revenue Bureau for collection.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with old salt profits before the reform, at four times current price in inflated valuation this would be more than seventeen million four hundred thousand strings; we request it be handed to the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 其年詔曰：「兩稅之法，悉委郡國，初極便人。

translations.literal: That year an edict said: "The two-tax law was entirely entrusted to prefectures and commanderies; at first it was extremely convenient for the people."
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict said: "The two-tax law was entrusted to prefectures and commanderies; at first it was extremely convenient for the people."

sentences.zh: 但緣約法之時，不定物估。

translations.literal: But because at the time the compact was made, commodity valuations were not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: But because at the time the compact was made, commodity valuations were not fixed.

sentences.zh: 今度支鹽鐵，泉貨是司，各有分巡，置於都會。

translations.literal: Now the Revenue Bureau and salt and iron office oversee currency; each has separate inspection tours stationed at major cities.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Revenue Bureau and salt and iron office oversee currency; each has inspection tours stationed at major cities.

sentences.zh: 爰命帖職，周視四方，簡而易從，庶葉權便。

translations.literal: We therefore appoint special commissioners to tour the four directions, simple and easy to follow, hoping to accord with expedient authority.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore appoint special commissioners to tour the four directions, simple and easy to follow, hoping to accord with expedient authority.

sentences.zh: 政有所弊，事有所宜，皆得舉聞，副我憂寄。

translations.literal: Where government has flaws or affairs require action, all may be reported upward, fulfilling Our entrusted concerns.
translations.idiomatic: Where government has flaws or affairs require action, all may be reported upward, fulfilling Our entrusted concerns.

sentences.zh: 以揚子鹽鐵留後為江淮已南兩稅使，江陵留後為荊衡漢沔東界、彭蠡已南兩稅使，度支山南西道分巡院官充三川兩稅使。

translations.literal: The Yangzi salt and iron rear commissioner was made two-tax commissioner for all south of Jiang-Huai; the Jiangling rear commissioner for Jing-Heng, east of Han and Mian, and south of Poyang; a Revenue Bureau Shannan West inspection official as Three Rivers two-tax commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi salt and iron rear commissioner was made two-tax commissioner for all south of Jiang-Huai; the Jiangling rear commissioner for Jing-Heng, east of Han and Mian, and south of Poyang; a revenue bureau Shannan west inspection official as Three Rivers two-tax commissioner.

sentences.zh: 峽內煎鹽五監先屬鹽鐵使，今宜割屬度支，便委山南西道兩稅使兼知糶賣。

translations.literal: The five boiled-salt directorates within the Gorges formerly belonged to the salt and iron commissioner; they should now be severed to the Revenue Bureau, with the Shannan West two-tax commissioner also managing sale and distribution.
translations.idiomatic: The five boiled-salt directorates within the gorges formerly belonged to salt and iron; they should now go to the Revenue Bureau, with the Shannan west two-tax commissioner also managing sales.

sentences.zh: 」峽內鹽屬度支，自此始也。

translations.literal: " Gorge salt belonging to the Revenue Bureau began from this.
translations.idiomatic: " Gorge salt belonging to the Revenue Bureau began here.

sentences.zh: 七年，王播奏去年鹽利除割峽內鹽，收錢六百八十五萬，從實估也。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Wang Bo memorialized that last year's salt profits, excluding gorge salt, collected six million eight hundred fifty thousand strings at real valuation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, Wang Bo memorialized that last year's salt profits, excluding gorge salt, collected six million eight hundred fifty thousand strings at real valuation.

sentences.zh: 又奏，商人于戶部、度支、鹽鐵三司飛錢，謂之「便換」。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that merchants at the Ministry of Revenue, Revenue Bureau, and salt and iron office used flying cash transfers, called "convenient exchange."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that merchants at the Ministry of Revenue, Revenue Bureau, and salt and iron office used flying cash transfers, called "convenient exchange."

sentences.zh: 八年，以崔倰為揚子留後、淮嶺已來兩稅使；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Cui Lin was made Yangzi rear commissioner and two-tax commissioner for all from Huai and Ling southward;
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, Cui Lin was made Yangzi rear commissioner and two-tax commissioner for all from Huai and Ling southward;

sentences.zh: 崔祝為江陵留後，為荊南已來兩稅使。

translations.literal: Cui Zhu was made Jiangling rear commissioner and two-tax commissioner for all from Jingnan southward.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhu was made Jiangling rear commissioner and two-tax commissioner for all from Jingnan southward.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，播又奏，以「軍興之時，財用是切。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year, Bo again memorialized: "When armies are raised, finances are urgent."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 13, Bo again memorialized: "When armies are raised, finances are urgent."

sentences.zh: 頃者劉晏領使，皆自按置租庸，至於州縣否臧，錢穀利病之物，虛實皆得而知。

translations.literal: Recently when Liu Yan led the commission, he personally arranged zu-yong; as to whether prefectures and counties were sound or corrupt, and matters of money, grain, benefit and harm, actual and nominal—all could be known.
translations.idiomatic: Recently when Liu Yan led the commission, he personally arranged zu-yong; whether prefectures and counties were sound or corrupt, and matters of money, grain, benefit and harm, actual and nominal—all could be known.

sentences.zh: 今臣守務在城，不得自往。

translations.literal: Now your subject's duties keep him in the city and he cannot go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Now my duties keep me in the city and I cannot go in person.

sentences.zh: 請令臣副使程異出巡江淮，其州府上供錢穀，一切勘問。

translations.literal: We request that your subject's vice commissioner Cheng Yi tour Jiang-Huai and investigate all money and grain the prefectures submit upward.
translations.idiomatic: I request that my vice commissioner Cheng Yi tour Jiang-Huai and investigate all money and grain the prefectures submit upward.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 閏五月，異至江淮，得錢一百八十五萬貫以進。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month, Yi reached Jiang-Huai and forwarded one million eight hundred fifty thousand strings in cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month, Yi reached Jiang-Huai and forwarded one million eight hundred fifty thousand strings in cash.

sentences.zh: 其年，以播守禮部尚書，以衛尉卿程異代之。

translations.literal: That year, Bo was made Minister of Rites on probation; Court of Imperial Entertainments Director Cheng Yi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Bo was made minister of rites on probation; Court of Imperial Entertainments director Cheng Yi replaced him.

sentences.zh: 十四年，異卒，以刑部侍郎柳公綽代之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Yi died; Vice Minister of Justice Liu Gongchuo replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, Yi died; justice vice minister Liu Gongchuo replaced him.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，王播復代公綽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, Wang Bo again replaced Gongchuo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changqing, Wang Bo again replaced Gongchuo.

sentences.zh: 四年，王涯以戶部侍郎代播。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Wang Ya as Vice Minister of Revenue replaced Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, Wang Ya as revenue vice minister replaced Bo.

sentences.zh: 敬宗初，播復以鹽鐵使為揚州節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingzong, Bo again served as salt and iron commissioner and Yangzhou Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingzong, Bo again served as salt and iron commissioner and Yangzhou military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，入覲，以宰相判使。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended, Bo came to audience and was made chief councilor judging the commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended, Bo came to audience and was made chief councilor judging the commission.

sentences.zh: 其後，王涯復判二使，表請使茶山之人移植根本，舊有貯積，皆使焚棄。

translations.literal: Thereafter Wang Ya again judged the two commissions and memorialized requesting that tea-mountain people transplant roots; old stores were all ordered burned and discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Wang Ya again judged the two commissions and memorialized that tea-mountain people transplant roots; old stores were all ordered burned.

sentences.zh: 天下怨之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven resented this.
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven resented this.

sentences.zh: 九年，涯以事誅。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Ya was executed for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, Ya was executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 而令狐楚以戶部尚書右僕射主之，以是年茶法大壞，奏請付州縣而入其租於戶部，人人悅焉。

translations.literal: Then Linghu Chu, as Minister of Revenue and Right Vice Director, presided over it; that year the tea law was greatly damaged; he memorialized requesting that [collection] be entrusted to prefectures and counties and that the rent be entered into the Revenue Ministry—everyone was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu then took charge as revenue minister and right vice director; that year the tea monopoly had collapsed. He memorialized to return collection to the prefectures and counties and to remit the levy to the Revenue Ministry, to universal approval.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，李石以中書侍郎判收茶法，復貞元之制也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng, Li Shi, as Vice Director of the Secretariat, judged collection of the tea law, restoring the Zhenyuan system.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 1 (836), Li Shi as secretariat vice director took charge of tea revenue and restored the Zhenyuan regulations.

sentences.zh: 三年，以戶部尚書同平章事楊嗣復主之，多革前監院之陳事。

translations.literal: In the third year, Yang Sifu, as Minister of Revenue and Associate Chief Councilor, presided; he greatly abolished the stale practices of the former supervisory bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, Yang Sifu as revenue minister and associate chief councilor took over and swept away many entrenched abuses of the old supervisory office.

sentences.zh: 開成三年至大中壬申，凡一十五年，多任以元臣，以集其務。

translations.literal: From the third year of Kaicheng to the ren-shen year of Dazhong, altogether fifteen years, [the post] was mostly filled with senior ministers to gather its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From Kaicheng 3 (838) through Dazhong ren-shen (852)—fifteen years in all—the duty was usually given to leading ministers to keep the system in order.

sentences.zh: 崔珙自刑部尚書拜，杜忭以淮南節度領之，既而皆踐公台。

translations.literal: Cui Hong was appointed from the post of Minister of Justice; Du Fu led it while holding the Huainan commission; both later reached the chief councilor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong was promoted from minister of justice; Du Fu held the post concurrently as Huainan commissioner—both men later rose to chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 薛元賞、李執方、盧弘正、馬植、敬晦五人，於九年之中，相踵理之，植亦自是居相位。

translations.literal: The five men Xue Yuanshang, Li Zhifang, Lu Hongzheng, Ma Zhi, and Jing Hui, within nine years, succeeded one another in managing it; Zhi also from then on held the chief councilor's position.
translations.idiomatic: Over nine years Xue Yuanshang, Li Zhifang, Lu Hongzheng, Ma Zhi, and Jing Hui ran the office in succession; Ma Zhi himself later entered the chief councilorate.

sentences.zh: 大中五年二月，以戶部侍郎裴休為鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Dazhong, Pei Xiu, as Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Dazhong 5 (851), revenue vice minister Pei Xiu was appointed salt and iron transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，以本官平章事，依前判使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year, with his original office he was made Chief Councilor, continuing as before to judge the commission.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the eighth month, he was made chief councilor while retaining his post and continued to direct the commission as before.

sentences.zh: 始者，漕米歲四十萬斛，其能至渭倉者，十不三四。

translations.literal: At the outset, transport grain each year was four hundred thousand piculs; of what could reach the Wei granary, not three or four in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Originally four hundred thousand piculs of tribute grain were shipped annually, yet fewer than three or four tenths ever reached the Wei granary.

sentences.zh: 漕吏狡蠹，敗溺百端，官舟之沉，多者歲至七十餘隻。

translations.literal: Transport clerks were crafty and corrupt; losses and sinkings took every form; official boats that sank—in many years reached more than seventy vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Transport clerks cheated and plundered; spoilage and foundering took every form; in bad years more than seventy government barges went down.

sentences.zh: 緣河奸犯，大紊晏法。

translations.literal: Wicked offenders along the river greatly disrupted Yan's methods.
translations.idiomatic: Riverine bandits and smugglers thoroughly wrecked the transport system Yan had perfected.

sentences.zh: 休使僚屬按之，委河次縣令董之。

translations.literal: Xiu sent his subordinates to investigate and entrusted river-bank county magistrates to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu sent staff to investigate and put riverine county magistrates in charge of supervision.

sentences.zh: 自江津達渭，以四十萬斛之傭，計緡二十八萬，悉使歸諸漕吏。

translations.literal: From the river crossing to the Wei, for the labor pay on four hundred thousand piculs, calculating two hundred eighty thousand strings of cash, he had it all returned to the transport clerks.
translations.idiomatic: For haulage from the Yangtze crossing to the Wei—pay on four hundred thousand piculs totaling two hundred eighty thousand strings—he ordered the full sum paid to the transport clerks themselves.

sentences.zh: 巡院胥吏，無得侵牟。

translations.literal: Patrol-bureau clerks were not permitted to encroach and extort.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol-office clerks were forbidden to skim or squeeze the carriers.

sentences.zh: 舉之為法，凡十事，奏之。

translations.literal: He raised these as regulations—altogether ten matters—and memorialized them.
translations.idiomatic: He codified ten measures in all and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，又立稅茶之法，凡十二條，陳奏。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year, he again established a tea-tax law—altogether twelve articles—and presented a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 6 he also framed a tea tax law in twelve articles and memorialized it.

sentences.zh: 上大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「裴休興利除害，深見奉公。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Pei Xiu promotes profit and removes harm; he deeply shows devotion to the public good.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "Pei Xiu has increased revenue and cut abuses; his loyalty to the public interest is plain.

sentences.zh: 」盡可其奏。

translations.literal: " All his memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Every article of his proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 由是三歲漕米至渭濱，積一百二十萬斛，無升合沉棄焉。

translations.literal: From this, in three years transport grain reached the Wei bank; they accumulated one million two hundred thousand piculs, without a sheng or he discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years grain reached the Wei in full; stocks rose to 1.2 million piculs without losing so much as a cupful overboard.

sentences.zh: 武德元年九月四日，置社倉。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the ninth month of the first year of Wude, community granaries were established.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth month's fourth day in Wude 1 (618), community granaries were established.

sentences.zh: 其月二十二日詔曰：「特建農圃，本督耕耘，思俾齊民，既康且富。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of that month an edict said: "Specially establish agricultural gardens, originally to supervise plowing and harrowing, thinking to make the common people prosperous and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two days later an edict declared: "Let farming colonies be founded to oversee tillage, so that the people may live in plenty and peace.

sentences.zh: 鐘庾之量，冀同水火。

translations.literal: The measure of bell-granaries—may it be like fire and water [in abundance].
translations.idiomatic: May grain reserves become as plentiful as fire and water.

sentences.zh: 宜置常平監官，以均天下之貨。

translations.literal: It is fitting to establish ever-normal supervisory officials to equalize goods under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-normal commissioners should be appointed to stabilize prices throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 市肆騰踴，則減價而出；

translations.literal: When markets surge in price, then reduce the price and release [grain];
translations.idiomatic: When markets run high, sell from stores at reduced prices;

sentences.zh: 田穡豐羨，則增糴而收。

translations.literal: when fields are abundant in harvest, then increase purchase and collect.
translations.idiomatic: when harvests are rich, buy in at higher rates.

sentences.zh: 庶使公私俱濟，家給人足，抑止兼併，宣通壅滯。

translations.literal: May it make public and private both aided, households provided and people sufficient, suppress annexation, and unclog stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus public and private interests alike would be served, households would be stocked, monopolists checked, and hoarding relieved.

sentences.zh: 」至五年十二月，廢常平監官。

translations.literal: " By the twelfth month of the fifth year [the offices] were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " By the twelfth month of year 5 the ever-normal supervisors were abolished.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年四月，尚書左丞戴胄上言曰：「水旱凶災，前聖之所不免。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Zhenguan, Left Vice Director Dai Zhou submitted: "Floods, droughts, and disasters—former sages could not avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhenguan 2 (628), left vice director Dai Zhou memorialized: "Flood, drought, and famine are what even the sages could not escape.

sentences.zh: 國無九年儲畜，《禮經》之所明誡。

translations.literal: A state without nine years' stored grain—the Rites Classic makes this an explicit warning.
translations.idiomatic: A state without nine years' reserves violates what the Book of Rites plainly requires.

sentences.zh: 今喪亂之後，戶口凋殘，每歲納租，未實倉廩。

translations.literal: Now after the disorders, households are depleted and ruined; each year's delivered rent does not truly fill the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: After the civil wars population is shattered; annual tax grain no longer truly fills the bins.

sentences.zh: 隨時出給，才供當年，若有凶災，將何賑恤？

translations.literal: Issuing out as the seasons require barely supplies the current year—if disaster strikes, with what will relief be provided?
translations.idiomatic: Current outlays barely cover the year—what reserve remains if famine returns?

sentences.zh: 故隋開皇立制，天下之人，節級輸粟，多為社倉，終於文皇，得無饑饉。

translations.literal: Therefore in Kaihuang of Sui a system was established: people under Heaven paid grain by graded quotas; many community granaries were made; down to Emperor Wen there was no famine.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Sui's Kaihuang reforms: graded grain quotas from the populace, community granaries everywhere—through Wen's reign famine was unknown.

sentences.zh: 及大業中年，國用不足，並貸社倉之物，以充官費，故至末塗，無以支給。

translations.literal: By the middle of the Daye reign, state use was insufficient; community-granary goods were all lent to meet official expenses—so by the final stage there was nothing to disburse.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Daye the treasury ran dry; community stores were lent to cover official costs until nothing was left to disburse.

sentences.zh: 今請自王公已下，爰及眾庶，計所墾田稼穡頃畝，至秋熟，准其見在苗以理勸課，盡令出粟。

translations.literal: Now I request that from kings and dukes down to the common multitude, calculating the mu of fields plowed and crops sown, when autumn ripens, according to standing grain encourage collection, and entirely order grain turned out.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that from princes to commoners, once autumn ripening is assessed by acreage, all be urged to contribute grain according to the crop in the field.

sentences.zh: 稻麥之鄉，亦同此稅。

translations.literal: In districts of rice, wheat, and millet, the same tax applies.
translations.idiomatic: Rice, wheat, and millet districts would follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 各納所在，為言義倉。

translations.literal: Each pays into his locality; call it the charity granary.
translations.idiomatic: Contributions would stay local under the name "charity granary."

sentences.zh: 若年谷不登，百姓饑饉，當所州縣，隨便取給。

translations.literal: If the year's grain does not mature and the people hunger, the prefecture and county concerned shall take and issue as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: If harvest fails and people starve, the local prefecture or county would draw on the store for relief.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「既為百姓預作儲貯，官為舉掌，以備凶年，非朕所須，橫生賦斂。

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "Since it is for the people to prepare storage in advance, and the state to hold it in charge against bad years, it is not what I require by imposing levies.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong replied: "Let the people build reserves the state will guard for lean years—not a new tax levied for my sake.

sentences.zh: 利人之事，深是可嘉。

translations.literal: A matter that profits the people is deeply praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: A policy that truly benefits the people deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 宜下所司，議立條制。

translations.literal: It is fitting to send down to the relevant offices to deliberate and establish regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Have the ministries draft regulations accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」戶部尚書韓仲良奏：「王公已下墾田，畝納二升。

translations.literal: " Minister of Revenue Han Zhongliang memorialized: "For kings and dukes down, on each mu of reclaimed field, two sheng per mu are paid.
translations.idiomatic: " Revenue minister Han Zhongliang proposed two sheng per mu on all reclaimed land from princes downward.

sentences.zh: 其粟麥粳稻之屬，各依土地。

translations.literal: Rice, wheat, millet, and the like—each according to the land.
translations.idiomatic: Rice, wheat, millet, and other grains would follow local custom.

sentences.zh: 貯之州縣，以備凶年。

translations.literal: Store in prefectures and counties against famine years.
translations.idiomatic: Grain would be held in prefectural and county stores against famine.

sentences.zh: 」可之。

translations.literal: " [This was] approved.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 自是天下州縣，始置義倉，每有饑饉，則開倉賑給。

translations.literal: From this, prefectures and counties under Heaven first established charity granaries; whenever famine struck, they opened the granaries and gave relief.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter charity granaries spread through the empire; in famine years the bins were opened for relief.

sentences.zh: 以至高宗、則天，數十年間，義倉不許雜用。

translations.literal: Down to Gaozong and Empress Zetian, for several decades charity-granary goods were not permitted for mixed use.
translations.idiomatic: Through Gaozong and Wu Zetian's reigns—decades—charity stores could not be diverted to other uses.

sentences.zh: 其後公私窘迫，漸貸義倉支用。

translations.literal: Afterward, when public and private were straitened, they gradually borrowed charity-granary goods for expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as public and private coffers tightened, charity grain was gradually borrowed for routine spending.

sentences.zh: 自中宗神龍之後，天下義倉費用向盡。

translations.literal: From after Zhongzong's Shenlong reign, charity granaries under Heaven were nearly exhausted in use.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongzong's Shenlong era the empire's charity reserves were largely spent.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽二年六月，敕：「義倉據地收稅，實是勞煩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Yonghui, an edict: "Charity granaries' tax by land area is truly laborious and troublesome.
