translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yonghui 2 (651) an edict noted: "Levying charity grain by acreage is burdensome.

sentences.zh: 宜令率戶出粟，上上戶五石，餘各有差。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order households by rate to turn out grain: upper-upper households five shi, the rest each with a difference.
translations.idiomatic: Households should instead contribute by rank—five shi from the wealthiest, less from others by grade.

sentences.zh: 」六年，京東西二市置常平倉。

translations.literal: " In the sixth year, ever-normal granaries were placed in the eastern and western markets of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " In year 6 ever-normal granaries were opened in the capital's eastern and western markets.

sentences.zh: 明慶二年十二月，京常平倉置常平署官員。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Xianqing, capital ever-normal granaries were given ever-normal bureau staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Xianqing 2 (657) the capital ever-normal stores received a dedicated bureau staff.

sentences.zh: 開元二年九月，敕：「天下諸州，今年稍熟，谷價全賤，或慮傷農。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Kaiyuan, an edict: "Prefectures under Heaven this year are somewhat ripe; grain prices are altogether cheap—or we fear harm to the farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 2, ninth month: an edict observed that many provinces had good harvests and grain was cheap—farmers risked ruin.

sentences.zh: 常平之法，行之自古，宜令諸州加時價三兩錢糴，不得抑斂。

translations.literal: The ever-normal method has been practiced since antiquity; it is fitting to order the prefectures to purchase at three cash above the seasonal price, and not to press down.
translations.idiomatic: The ever-normal system is ancient practice: provinces should buy at three cash above the market rate without coercion.

sentences.zh: 仍交相付領，勿許懸欠。

translations.literal: Still hand over and receive in turn; do not permit outstanding arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Payments must be settled promptly—no outstanding debts.

sentences.zh: 蠶麥時熟，谷米必貴，即令減價出糶。

translations.literal: When silkworms and wheat ripen, grain must be dear—then order reduced-price sale.
translations.idiomatic: When silk and wheat seasons peak and grain prices rise, sell from stores at reduced rates.

sentences.zh: 豆穀等堪貯者，熟亦准此。

translations.literal: Beans, grain, and what can be stored—when ripe, apply the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Beans and storable grains follow the same rule when harvest comes in.

sentences.zh: 以時出入，務在利人。

translations.literal: Release and take in according to the season, with the task of benefiting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Buy and sell in season solely to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 其常平所須錢物，宜令所司支料奏聞。

translations.literal: Money and goods required for the ever-normal [system]—it is fitting to order the relevant offices to disburse funds and report.
translations.idiomatic: Funds for ever-normal operations should be issued by the appropriate ministries on memorial.

sentences.zh: 」四年五月二十一日，詔：「諸州縣義倉，本備饑年賑給。

translations.literal: " On the twenty-first day of the fifth month of the fourth year, an edict: "Charity granaries in prefectures and counties were originally to prepare against famine years for relief.
translations.idiomatic: " On the twenty-first day of the fifth month in year 4 an edict recalled: "Prefectural charity granaries exist for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 近年已來，每三年一度，以百姓義倉糙米，遠赴京納，仍勒百姓私出腳錢。

translations.literal: In recent years, every three years once, coarse charity-grain rice from the people was sent far to the capital for delivery, and the people were still compelled to pay private porterage cash.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, every three years, charity brown rice was hauled to the capital while farmers were forced to pay cartage out of pocket.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，更不得義倉變造。

translations.literal: From now on, charity granaries must not again be converted [for capital shipment].
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth charity grain may no longer be diverted for capital shipment.

sentences.zh: 」七年六月，敕：「關內，隴右、河南、河北五道，及荊、揚、襄、夔、綿、益、彭、蜀，漢、劍、茂等州，並置常平倉。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month of the seventh year, an edict: "Within the Pass, Longyou, Henan, and Hebei five circuits, and Jing, Yang, Xiang, Kui, Mian, Yi, Peng, Shu, Han, Jian, Mao, and the like—all shall establish ever-normal granaries.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth month of year 7 an edict ordered ever-normal granaries throughout the Pass, Longyou, Henan, Hebei, and provinces including Jing, Yang, Xiang, Kui, Mian, Yi, Peng, Shu, Han, Jian, and Mao.

sentences.zh: 其本上州三千貫，中州二千貫，下州一千貫。

translations.literal: For these, upper prefectures three thousand strings, middle prefectures two thousand, lower prefectures one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Capital grants were set at three thousand strings for upper prefectures, two thousand for middle, one thousand for lower.

sentences.zh: 」十六年十月，敕：「自今歲普熟，穀價至賤，必恐傷農。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month of the sixteenth year, an edict: "This year is universally ripe; grain prices are extremely cheap—we must fear harm to the farmers.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month of year 16 another edict warned that universal harvest had driven prices so low that farmers would suffer.

sentences.zh: 加錢收糴，以實倉廩，縱逢水旱，不慮阻饑，公私之間，或亦為便。

translations.literal: Add cash and purchase grain to fill the granaries; even if flood or drought strike, we need not fear blocked famine; between public and private it may also be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Buy in at premium rates to fill the bins so that flood or drought need not mean starvation, to the benefit of state and people alike.

sentences.zh: 宜令所在以常平本錢及當處物，各於時價上量加三錢，百姓有糶易者，為收糴。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order each locality, with ever-normal principal funds and local goods, on the seasonal price to measure an addition of three cash; where the people have grain to sell, purchase for them.
translations.idiomatic: Local authorities should use ever-normal capital to buy at three cash above market wherever farmers offer grain.

sentences.zh: 事須兩和，不得限數。

translations.literal: The matter must be mutually agreed; do not fix quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Purchases must be voluntary—no forced quotas.

sentences.zh: 配糴訖，具所用錢物及所糴物數，申所司。

translations.literal: When purchase is finished, fully report the cash and goods used and the number of goods purchased to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: When buying is complete, report funds spent and grain taken to the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 仍令上佐一人專勾當。

translations.literal: Still order one senior aide to specialize in oversight.
translations.idiomatic: A senior aide in each prefecture was to oversee the operation.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載三月，太府少卿張瑄奏：「准四載五月並五載三月敕節文，至貴時賤價出糶，賤時加價收糴。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Tianbao, Vice Director of the Grand Storehouse Zhang Xuan memorialized: "According to the text of edicts in the fifth month of the fourth year and the third month of the fifth year—to sell when dear at cheap price, when cheap to purchase at added price.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianbao 6 (747), grand storehouse vice director Zhang Xuan cited prior edicts: sell when prices are high, buy when they are low.

sentences.zh: 若百姓未辦錢物者，任准開元二十年七月敕，量事賒糶，至粟麥熟時征納。

translations.literal: If the people have not prepared cash and goods, permit according to the seventh-month edict of the twentieth year of Kaiyuan to grant credit sale as the matter requires, and collect when millet and wheat ripen.
translations.idiomatic: Where households lacked cash, Kaiyuan 20's edict allowed credit sales to be repaid at harvest.

sentences.zh: 臣使司商量，且糶舊糴新，不同別用。

translations.literal: Your servant's office deliberated: for the present sell old and buy new—not to use differently.
translations.idiomatic: His office proposed rotating old stock with new purchases rather than mingling accounts.

sentences.zh: 其賒糶者，至納錢日若粟麥雜種等時價甚賤，恐更回易艱辛，請加價便與折納。

translations.literal: For those on credit sale, on the day of paying cash if millet, wheat, and mixed grains' seasonal prices are very cheap—we fear exchange will again be arduous; I request adding price and permitting offset payment.
translations.idiomatic: When repayment fell in a cheap market, farmers faced hardship; he asked that repayment accept grain at a premium valuation.

sentences.zh: 」廣德二年正月，第五琦奏：「每州常平倉及庫使司，商量置本錢，隨當處米物時價，賤則加價收糴，貴則減價糶賣。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the second year of Guangde, Diwu Qi memorialized: "Each prefecture's ever-normal granary and treasury office should deliberate setting principal funds; according to local grain and goods' seasonal price—when cheap add price and purchase, when dear reduce price and sell.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first month of Guangde 2 (763) Diwu Qi urged each province to fund ever-normal granaries and buy low, sell high according to local prices.

sentences.zh: 建中元年七月，敕：「夫常平者，常使谷價如一，大豐不為之減，大儉不為之加。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Jianzhong, an edict: "The ever-normal [system] constantly keeps grain prices as one; in great abundance it does not reduce them, in great scarcity it does not raise them.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong 1, seventh month: an edict defined ever-normal policy as holding grain prices steady—neither depressed in bumper years nor inflated in dearth.

sentences.zh: 雖遇災荒，人無菜色。

translations.literal: Even if disaster and famine are encountered, the people have no vegetable pallor.
translations.idiomatic: Even in disaster the people would not go hungry.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，忽米價貴時，宜量出官米十萬石，麥十萬石，每日量付兩市行人下價糶貨。

translations.literal: From now on, whenever grain prices suddenly become dear, it is fitting to measure and release one hundred thousand shi of government rice and one hundred thousand shi of wheat, each day measured and entrusted to the two markets' brokers to sell at reduced price.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever prices spiked, the state should release one hundred thousand shi each of rice and wheat daily to the capital markets for sale below market.

sentences.zh: 」三年九月，戶部侍郎趙贊上言曰：「伏以舊制，置倉儲粟，名曰常平。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month of the third year, Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan submitted: "I bow to observe the old system: establish granaries and store grain—called ever-normal.
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth month of year 3 revenue vice minister Zhao Zan memorialized: "The old system stored grain in ever-normal granaries.

sentences.zh: 軍興已來，此事闕廢，或因凶荒流散，餓死相食者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Since military campaigns began, this matter has been neglected and abandoned; some because of disaster and famine people scattered—those who starved and ate one another cannot be fully counted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebellions the system had lapsed; famine and flight had left countless dead who ate one another.

sentences.zh: 古者平准之法，使萬室之邑，必有萬鐘之藏，千室之邑，必有千鐘之藏，春以奉耕，夏以奉耘，雖有大賈富家，不得豪奪吾人者，蓋謂能行輕重之法也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the leveling-and-stabilization method: let a city of ten thousand households surely have ten thousand zhong stored; a city of a thousand households surely have a thousand zhong stored—spring to supply plowing, summer to supply hoeing—even if there are great merchants and wealthy houses, they cannot forcibly seize our people—this is called being able to practice the light-and-heavy method.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity's "balancing the markets" required ten thousand zhong for a city of ten thousand families, a thousand for a thousand—grain for spring plowing and summer weeding—so that even great merchants could not prey on the people: that is true control of supply.

sentences.zh: 自陛下登極以來，許京城兩市置常平，官糴鹽米，雖經頻年少雨，米價未騰貴，此乃即自明驗，實要推而廣之。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended, permission was granted to establish ever-normal [offices] in the capital's two markets; the state purchased salt and rice—even through years of frequent little rain, rice prices did not surge dear; this is itself clear proof and truly should be extended and broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession ever-normal offices in the two capital markets have stabilized salt and grain—even in drought years prices did not spike. The proof is plain; the policy should be extended empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 當軍興之時，與承平或異，事須兼儲布帛，以備時須。

translations.literal: In times of military campaigns versus peaceful times, the matter must also store cloth and silk against timely need.
translations.idiomatic: Wartime needs differ from peace: cloth and silk must be stockpiled as well.

sentences.zh: 臣今商量，請於兩都並江陵、成都、揚、汴、蘇、洪等州府，各置常平，輕重本錢，上至百萬貫，下至數十萬貫，隨其所宜，量定多少。

translations.literal: Your servant now deliberates and requests that at the two capitals together with Jiangling, Chengdu, Yang, Bian, Su, Hong, and other prefectures, each establish ever-normal [offices]; light-and-heavy principal funds from up to one million strings down to several hundred thousand strings—as each place suits, measure and fix the amount.
translations.idiomatic: I propose ever-normal offices at both capitals and major centers—Jiangling, Chengdu, Yangzhou, Bianzhou, Suzhou, Hongzhou—with capital from one million strings down to several hundred thousand as local conditions require.

sentences.zh: 唯貯斛鬥疋段絲麻等，候物貴則下價出賣，物賤則加價收糴。

translations.literal: Only store piculs, bolts of cloth, silk, and hemp; wait until goods are dear then sell at reduced price, when goods are cheap then purchase at added price.
translations.idiomatic: They would hold grain, cloth, silk, and hemp—selling when prices rose, buying when they fell.

sentences.zh: 權其輕重，以利疲人。

translations.literal: Weigh the light and heavy to benefit the weary people.
translations.idiomatic: Regulate supply to relieve the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The throne] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 贊於是條奏諸道津要都會之所，皆置吏，閱商人財貨。

translations.literal: Zan thereupon itemized and memorialized that at every circuit's strategic passes and great market towns, officials should be placed to inspect merchants' goods and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Zan then ordered agents at every major pass and market to inventory merchant wealth.

sentences.zh: 計錢每貫稅二十，天下所出竹、木、茶、漆，皆十一稅之，以充常平本。

translations.literal: Calculating cash, twenty per string were taxed; all bamboo, wood, tea, and lacquer produced under Heaven were taxed one in ten to fill the ever-normal principal.
translations.idiomatic: A tax of twenty cash per string was levied; bamboo, timber, tea, and lacquer nationwide were taxed ten percent to capitalize the ever-normal fund.

sentences.zh: 時國用稍廣，常賦不足，所稅亦隨時而盡，終不能為常平本。

translations.literal: At the time state use was somewhat broad; regular levies were insufficient; the taxes also in time were exhausted—ultimately they could not serve as ever-normal principal.
translations.idiomatic: State spending soon outran revenue; the new levies were spent as fast as collected and never built a lasting ever-normal reserve.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年十月，敕：「諸軍鎮和糴貯備，共三十三萬石，價之外，更量與優饒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Zhenyuan, an edict: "Army posts' harmonized purchases for storage—altogether three hundred thirty thousand shi; beyond the price, further measure and grant preferential bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan 8, tenth month: an edict ordered army districts to stock three hundred thirty thousand shi through harmonized purchase, paying above market and adding a premium.

sentences.zh: 其粟及麻，據米數准折虛價，直委度支，以停江淮運腳錢充，並支綾絹、糸絁、綿，勿令折估。

translations.literal: The millet and hemp, according to rice quantity converted at nominal price, directly entrusted to the Revenue Bureau, using suspended Jiang-Huai transport porterage cash to cover it, and disbursing silk, gauze, and cotton—do not permit depreciated valuation.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and hemp were to be valued against rice and paid through the Revenue Bureau from suspended Yangtze transport funds in silk, gauze, and cotton without discounting.

sentences.zh: 所糴粟等，委本道節度使監軍同勾當別貯，非承特敕，不得給用。

translations.literal: The purchased grain and the like—entrust the circuit military commissioner and army supervisor jointly to check and separately store; without receiving a special edict, do not permit issuance for use.
translations.idiomatic: Purchased grain was to be stored under joint supervision of commissioners and army supervisors and issued only on special order.

sentences.zh: 」十四年六月，詔以米價稍貴，令度支出官米十萬石，於兩街賤糶。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month of the fourteenth year, an edict: because rice prices were somewhat dear, order the Revenue Bureau to release one hundred thousand shi of government rice in the two wards for cheap sale.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth month of year 14, as rice prices rose, the Revenue Bureau released one hundred thousand shi for cheap sale in the two capital wards.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，以歲饑，出太倉粟三十萬石出糶。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, because the year was famine-stricken, release three hundred thousand shi from the Grand Granary for sale.
translations.idiomatic: That September, famine prompted release of three hundred thousand shi from the Grand Granary.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬，河南府谷貴人流，令以含嘉倉粟七萬石出糶。

translations.literal: That winter, in Henan prefecture grain was dear and people fled; order seven hundred thousand shi from the Hejia Granary released for sale.
translations.idiomatic: That winter dearth in Henan drove migration; seven hundred thousand shi from the Hejia granary were sold off.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，以久旱歲饑，出太倉粟十八萬石，于諸縣賤糶。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year, because of long drought and famine in the year, release one hundred eighty thousand shi from the Grand Granary for cheap sale in the various counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 15 prolonged drought and famine led to release of one hundred eighty thousand shi from the Grand Granary for cheap sale in the counties.

sentences.zh: 元和元年正月，制：「歲時有豐歉，穀價有重輕，將備水旱之虞，在權聚斂之術。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yuanhe, an ordinance: "The seasons have abundance and shortage; grain prices have weight and lightness; to prepare against flood and drought's concern lies in the expedient art of gathering and storing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanhe 1 (806) an edict declared: "Harvests rise and fall, grain prices swing—guarding against flood and drought requires prudent storage policy.

sentences.zh: 應天下州府每年所稅地子數內，宜十分取二分，均充常平倉及義倉，仍各逐穩便收貯，以時出糶，務在救人，賑貸所宜，速奏。

translations.literal: All prefectures under Heaven within the annual land-tax grain amounts—it is fitting to take two in ten, evenly to fill ever-normal granaries and charity granaries; still each follow convenient storage, release grain in season, with the task of saving people; relief and lending as appropriate—memorialize promptly.
translations.idiomatic: From each province's annual land-tax grain, two-tenths should fund ever-normal and charity granaries, stored locally and sold or lent in season to save lives—report promptly on relief needs.

sentences.zh: 」六年二月，制：「如聞京畿之內，舊穀已盡，宿麥未登，宜以常平、義倉粟二十四萬石貸借百姓。

translations.literal: " In the second month of the sixth year, an ordinance: "As we hear, within the capital region old grain is exhausted and winter wheat not yet ripe—it is fitting to lend two hundred forty thousand shi from ever-normal and charity granaries to the people.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second month of year 6 another edict noted that the capital's old stocks were gone and winter wheat not yet in: two hundred forty thousand shi from ever-normal and charity stores were to be lent to the people.

sentences.zh: 諸道州府有乏少糧種處，亦委所在官長，用常平、義倉米借貸。

translations.literal: In circuit prefectures where seed grain is scarce, also entrust the local chief officials to lend ever-normal and charity rice.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever provinces lacked seed grain, local officials were to lend ever-normal and charity rice as well.

sentences.zh: 淮南、浙西、宣歙等道，元和二年四月賑貸，並且停征。

translations.literal: Huainan, western Zhe, and Xuanshe circuits—in the fourth month of the second year of Yuanhe relief lending was granted, and tax collection was also suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan, western Zhe, and Xuanshe received relief loans in the fourth month of Yuanhe 2 (807), with collection suspended.

sentences.zh: 容至豐年，然後填納。

translations.literal: Permit repayment when the year is abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Repayment could wait until harvest was full.

sentences.zh: 」九年四月，詔出太倉粟七十萬石，開六場糶之，並賑貸外縣百姓。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month of the ninth year, an edict released seven hundred thousand shi from the Grand Granary, opened six markets to sell grain, and also gave relief loans to outer-county people.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth month of year 9 the throne released seven hundred thousand shi from the Grand Granary, opened six sale depots, and extended relief loans to suburban counties.

sentences.zh: 至秋熟征納，便於外縣收貯，以防水旱。

translations.literal: When autumn ripens collect payment; then conveniently store in outer counties against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: Repayment would come at autumn harvest, with grain held in outer counties against future dearth.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，詔出粟二十五萬石，分兩街降估出糶。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year, an edict released two hundred fifty thousand shi of grain, divided between the two wards for reduced-valuation sale.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 12 two hundred fifty thousand shi were released for discounted sale in the two capital wards.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，詔諸道應遭水州府，河中、澤潞、河東、幽州、江陵府等管內，及鄭、滑、滄、景、易、定、陳、許、晉、顯、蘇、襄、復、台、越、唐、隨、鄧等州人戶，宜令本州厚加優恤。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, an edict: circuits' prefectures that should suffer flood—within the jurisdictions of Hezhong, Zelu, Hedong, Youzhou, Jiangling prefecture, and prefectures Zheng, Hua, Cang, Jing, Yi, Ding, Chen, Xu, Jin, Xian, Su, Xiang, Fu, Tai, Yue, Tang, Sui, Deng, and the like—the households should be thickly given preferential care by their prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That September edicts ordered generous relief for flood-struck provinces including Hezhong, Zelu, Hedong, Youzhou, Jiangling, and dozens of afflicted prefectures from Zheng through Deng.

sentences.zh: 仍各以當處義倉斛鬥，據所損多少，量事賑給。

translations.literal: Still each use local charity-granary grain, according to damage more or less, measure the matter and give relief.
translations.idiomatic: Each locality was to draw on charity granaries and distribute grain in proportion to losses.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，戶部侍郎孟簡奏：「天下州府常平、義倉等斛鬥，請准舊例減估出糶，但以石數奏申，有司更不收管，州縣得專達以利百姓。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year, Vice Minister of Revenue Meng Jian memorialized: "Ever-normal and charity granaries' grain in prefectures under Heaven—I request according to old precedent reduced-valuation sale; only report the shi count; the relevant offices need not again take charge—prefectures and counties may act directly to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 13 revenue vice minister Meng Jian proposed that provinces sell ever-normal and charity grain at reduced rates per old custom, reporting only quantities while counties acted directly for the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The throne] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年二月，敕出太倉陳粟三十萬石，於兩街出糶。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Changqing, an edict released three hundred thousand shi of aged grain from the Grand Granary for sale in the two wards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Changqing 4 (824) three hundred thousand shi of aged Grand Granary grain were sold in the capital markets.

sentences.zh: 其年三月制曰：「義倉之制，其來日久。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year an ordinance said: "The charity-granary system—its origin is long-standing.
translations.idiomatic: That third month an edict observed that the charity-granary system was ancient.

sentences.zh: 近歲所在盜用沒入，致使小有水旱，生人坐委溝壑。

translations.literal: In recent years localities have stolen and embezzled it; causing even small flood or drought, the living sit abandoned in ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Lately local officials had stolen and diverted the stores, so that even minor disasters left people dying in ditches.

sentences.zh: 永言其弊，職此之由。

translations.literal: Ever speaking of its harm—the office lies in this cause.
translations.idiomatic: The fault lay entirely in maladministration.

sentences.zh: 宜令諸州錄事參軍，專主勾當。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order each prefecture's recording adjutant to specialize in oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture's recording adjutant was to oversee the granaries exclusively.

sentences.zh: 苟為長吏迫制，即許驛表上聞。

translations.literal: If compelled by the chief magistrate, he is permitted to memorialize urgently to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: If the prefect interfered, he might lodge an urgent memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 考滿之日，戶部差官交割。

translations.literal: On the day his term evaluation ends, the Revenue Ministry sends an official to hand over accounts.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end the Revenue Ministry would audit the accounts.

sentences.zh: 如無欠負，與減一選。

translations.literal: If there is no shortage, grant reduction of one selection.
translations.idiomatic: A clean handover earned one step toward promotion.

sentences.zh: 如欠少者，量加一選。

translations.literal: If the shortage is small, accordingly add one selection.
translations.idiomatic: Minor shortages cost one step on the promotion ladder.

sentences.zh: 欠數過多，戶部奏聞，節級科處。

translations.literal: If the shortage number is excessive, the Revenue Ministry memorializes to the throne and applies graded penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Large deficits were reported to the throne for graded punishment.

sentences.zh: 」大和四年八月，敕：「今年秋稼似熟，宜於關內七州府及鳳翔府和糴一百萬石。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe, an edict: "This year's autumn crops seem ripe; it is fitting in the seven prefectures within the Pass and Fengxiang prefecture to harmonize-purchase one million shi.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth month of Taihe 4 (830) an edict ordered one million shi purchased in the seven Pass prefectures and Fengxiang as the autumn harvest looked strong.

sentences.zh: 」大中六年四月，戶部奏：「諸州府常平、義倉斛鬥，本防水旱，賑貸百姓。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Dazhong, the Revenue Ministry memorialized: "Prefectures' ever-normal and charity granary grain originally guards against flood and drought and gives relief loans to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Dazhong 6 (852) the Revenue Ministry noted that ever-normal and charity stores existed for disaster relief.

sentences.zh: 其有災沴州府地遠，申奏往復，已至流亡。

translations.literal: Where there are disaster-struck prefectures far from the capital, memorializing back and forth already reaches flight and exile.
translations.idiomatic: In distant disaster provinces the memorial cycle itself drove people to flee before aid arrived.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，諸道遭災旱，請委所在長吏，差清強官審勘，如實有水旱處，便任先從貧下不支濟戶給貸。

translations.literal: From now on, wherever circuits suffer disaster or drought, I request entrusting the local chief official to send able, upright officials to investigate; if there truly is flood or drought, then permit first giving loans to the poorest households unable to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth local chiefs in stricken circuits should send reliable officers to verify damage and lend first to the poorest households before reporting.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The throne] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 建中四年六月，戶部侍郎趙贊請置大田：天下田計其頃畝，官收十分之一。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Jianzhong, Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan requested establishing great fields: calculating fields under Heaven by mu, the state collects one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jianzhong 4 (783) revenue vice minister Zhao Zan proposed "great fields": surveying empire-wide acreage and taking one-tenth for the state.

sentences.zh: 擇其上腴，樹桑環之，曰公桑。

translations.literal: Select the richest soil, plant mulberry trees around it—called public mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: The best land would be ringed with mulberry plantings as "public mulberry" plots.

sentences.zh: 自王公至於匹庶，差借其力，得穀絲以給國用。

translations.literal: From kings and dukes down to commoners, lend their labor by graded levy, obtaining grain and silk to supply state use.
translations.idiomatic: From princes to commoners labor would be conscripted by rank to supply grain and silk to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 詔從其說。

translations.literal: An edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 贊熟計之，自以為非便，皆寢不下。

translations.literal: Zan carefully calculated it and himself judged it inconvenient; all were shelved and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Zan reconsidered, found the scheme impractical, and let it die unpublished.

sentences.zh: 復請行常平稅茶之法。

translations.literal: He again requested implementing the ever-normal tea-tax law.
translations.idiomatic: He revived the ever-normal tea tax instead.

sentences.zh: 又以軍須迫蹙，常平利不時集，乃請稅屋間架、算除陌錢。

translations.literal: Also because military needs were pressing and ever-normal profits did not gather in time, he then requested taxing building frames and calculating transaction-removal cash.
translations.idiomatic: As military costs mounted and ever-normal funds lagged, he also proposed a building-frame tax and a transaction surcharge.

sentences.zh: 間架法：凡屋兩架為一間，至有貴賤，約價三等，上價間出錢二千，中價一千，下價五百。

translations.literal: The frame method: every two roof-beams frames count as one bay; up to noble and base, roughly three price grades—upper grade bays pay two thousand cash, middle one thousand, lower five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The frame tax counted every two roof-beams as one bay, graded by value: two thousand cash for high-value structures, one thousand for middle, five hundred for low.

sentences.zh: 所由吏秉算執籌，入人之廬舍而計其數。

translations.literal: The responsible clerks held counting rods and entered people's dwellings to calculate the number.
translations.idiomatic: Tax clerks with counting rods entered homes room by room.

sentences.zh: 衣冠士族，或貧無他財，獨守故業，坐多屋出算者，動數十萬。

translations.literal: Gentry clans, some poor without other wealth, solely keeping old estates—sitting with many bays subject to calculation, the amounts often reached several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry families clinging to ancestral houses with many bays faced assessments running into hundreds of thousands of cash.

sentences.zh: 人不勝其苦。

translations.literal: People could not bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: The burden was unbearable.

sentences.zh: 凡沒一間者，仗六十，告者賞錢五十貫，取於其家。

translations.literal: For every one bay concealed, sixty blows with the staff; informers rewarded fifty strings of cash, taken from the household.
translations.idiomatic: Concealing a bay brought sixty strokes; informers received fifty strings from the offender's household.

sentences.zh: 除陌法：天下公私給與貨易，率一貫舊算二十，益加算為五十。

translations.literal: The transaction-removal method: all public and private gifts and trade under Heaven—formerly one string taxed twenty, now increased to fifty.
translations.idiomatic: The transaction tax raised the levy on every string of cash in trade from twenty to fifty.

sentences.zh: 給與他物或兩換者，約錢為率算之。

translations.literal: When giving other goods or bartering two ways, estimate cash as the rate and calculate.
translations.idiomatic: Barter and in-kind payments were converted to cash value for taxation.

sentences.zh: 市牙各給印紙，人有買賣，隨自署記，翌日合算之。

translations.literal: Each market broker was given stamped paper; when people bought and sold they signed themselves; the next day it was totaled for calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Market brokers issued stamped slips; buyers and sellers recorded trades for next-day reckoning.

sentences.zh: 有自貿易不用市牙者，驗其私簿。

translations.literal: Those who traded on their own without using market brokers—their private ledgers were inspected.
translations.idiomatic: Traders bypassing brokers had private account books inspected.

sentences.zh: 無私簿者，投狀自集。

translations.literal: Those without private ledgers submitted statements to assemble [the record].
translations.idiomatic: Those without books filed sworn statements.

sentences.zh: 其有隱錢百者沒入，二千杖六十，告者賞十千，取其家資。

translations.literal: For concealing one hundred cash, confiscation; two thousand, sixty blows; informers rewarded ten thousand, taken from household assets.
translations.idiomatic: Hiding one hundred cash meant confiscation; two thousand brought sixty strokes; informers received ten thousand from the offender's assets.

sentences.zh: 法既行，而主人市牙得專其柄，率多隱盜。

translations.literal: Once the law was in force, house owners and market brokers monopolized its handle; mostly they concealed and embezzled.
translations.idiomatic: Once enacted, landlords and brokers controlled the system and skimmed most of the proceeds.

sentences.zh: 公家所入，曾不得半，而怨惸之聲，囂然滿於天下。

translations.literal: What the public treasury received did not reach half, while sounds of resentment and loneliness clamored throughout the land.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury captured less than half the nominal yield while outrage spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 至興元二年正月一日赦，悉停罷。

translations.literal: By the general amnesty of the first day of the first month of the second year of Xingyuan, all were stopped and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The general amnesty of Xingyuan 2, first month, first day (785) abolished both taxes.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年正月，初稅茶。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan, tea was first taxed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhenyuan 9 (793) the tea tax began.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸道鹽鐵使張滂奏曰：「伏以去歲水災，詔令減稅。

translations.literal: Before this, circuit salt-and-iron commissioner Zhang Peng memorialized: "I bow to observe that last year there was flood disaster; an edict ordered tax reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier salt and iron commissioner Zhang Peng had memorialized: "Last year's floods prompted tax relief.

sentences.zh: 今之國用，須有供儲。

translations.literal: Now state expenditures require provision and storage.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the treasury still needs revenue.

sentences.zh: 伏請於出茶州縣，及茶山外商人要路，委所由定三等時估，每十稅一，充所放兩稅。

translations.literal: I bow to request that at tea-exporting prefectures and counties, and at key routes outside tea mountains for merchants, entrust the responsible officials to fix three grades of seasonal price; every ten tax one, to cover the two taxes remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a ten-percent levy at tea-producing counties and major merchant routes, priced in three grades by local officials, to offset the remitted two taxes.

sentences.zh: 其明年以後所得稅，外貯之。

translations.literal: From the following year onward, tax receipts beyond that were stored separately.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus collections after the first year would be banked separately.

sentences.zh: 若諸州遭水旱，賦稅不辦，以此代之。

translations.literal: If prefectures encounter flood or drought and cannot deliver taxes, use this to substitute.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces unable to pay land tax after disaster could draw on the fund.

sentences.zh: 」詔可之，仍委滂具處置條奏。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this and still entrusted Peng to draft implementing regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved and ordered Peng to draft detailed rules.

sentences.zh: 自此每歲得錢四十萬貫。

translations.literal: From this each year four hundred thousand strings of cash were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the levy yielded four hundred thousand strings annually.

sentences.zh: 然稅無虛歲，遭水旱處亦未嘗以錢拯贍。

translations.literal: Yet the tax had no year without collection; places that suffered flood or drought also never used the cash for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Collection never lapsed—yet disaster provinces never saw the money used for relief.

sentences.zh: 大和七年，御史台奏：「伏准大和三年十一月十八日赦文，天下除兩稅外，不得妄有科配，其擅加雜榷率，一切宜停，令御史台嚴加察訪者。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe, the Censorate memorialized: "I bow to the amnesty text of the eighteenth day of the eleventh month of the third year of Taihe: aside from the two taxes under Heaven, there must be no reckless levies; all unauthorized miscellaneous monopolies and rates are to stop; order the Censorate strictly to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 7 (833) the Censorate cited Taihe 3's amnesty forbidding levies beyond the two taxes and demanding strict investigation of illegal surcharges.

sentences.zh: 臣昨因嶺南道擅置竹綀場，稅法至重，害人頗深。

translations.literal: Your servant yesterday because the Lingnan circuit had rashly established a bamboo-fabric office—the tax law was extremely heavy and harmed people deeply.
translations.idiomatic: They cited Lingnan's bamboo-fabric monopoly as a recent example of crushing illegal surcharges.

sentences.zh: 伏請起今已後，應諸道自大和三年准赦文所停兩稅處科配雜榷率等復卻置者，仰敕至後十日內，具卻置事由聞奏，仍申台司。

translations.literal: I bow to request that from now on, wherever circuits since the Taihe third-year amnesty-stopped two-tax surcharges and miscellaneous monopolies and rates are re-established, within ten days after the edict arrives they must fully report the reason for re-establishment and still report to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Any circuit reviving banned levies must report within ten days of the edict's arrival and notify the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 每有出使郎官御史，便令嚴加察訪。

translations.literal: Whenever investigating censors or palace gentlemen go out, order them strictly to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Every dispatched censor was to investigate strictly.

sentences.zh: 苟有此色，本判官重加懲責，長吏奏聽進止。

translations.literal: If such exists, the responsible judge receives heavy punishment; the chief magistrate memorializes for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Violations would bring heavy punishment on supervising officials and imperial review of prefects.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The throne] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 九年十二月，左僕射令狐楚奏新置榷茶使額：「伏以江淮間數年以來，水旱疾疫，凋傷頗甚，愁歎未平。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the ninth year, Left Vice Director Linghu Chu memorialized on the newly established tea-monopoly commissioner title: "I bow to observe that in the Jiang-Huai region for several years there have been flood, drought, and plague; depletion and injury are quite severe; grief and sighing are not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 9 left vice director Linghu Chu attacked the new tea-monopoly commission: "The Jiang-Huai region has suffered years of flood, drought, and plague; the people are not yet recovered.

sentences.zh: 今夏及秋，稍較豐稔。

translations.literal: This summer and autumn are somewhat more abundant in ripening.
translations.idiomatic: This summer and autumn brought a somewhat better harvest.

sentences.zh: 方須惠恤，各使安存。

translations.literal: Just when favor and relief are needed, each should be made secure and preserved.
translations.idiomatic: They need relief and security, not new burdens.

sentences.zh: 昨者忽奏榷茶，實為蠹政。

translations.literal: Yesterday suddenly memorializing tea monopoly is truly a policy that harms the state.
translations.idiomatic: The sudden tea monopoly is ruinous policy.

sentences.zh: 蓋是王涯破滅將至，怨怒合歸。

translations.literal: Probably because Wang Ya's destruction was approaching, resentment and anger converged on him.
translations.idiomatic: It was likely Wang Ya's desperate bid as his fall approached, channeling public rage.

sentences.zh: 豈有令百姓移茶樹就官場中栽，摘茶葉於官場中造？

translations.literal: How could there be ordering the people to move tea trees into government yards to plant, and pick tea leaves in government yards to manufacture?
translations.idiomatic: Who would order farmers to uproot tea trees for government plantations and process leaves in state workshops?

sentences.zh: 有同兒戲，不近人情。

translations.literal: It is like children's play—not close to human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: It was childish and inhumane.

sentences.zh: 方有恩權，無敢沮議，朝班相顧而失色，道路以目而吞聲。

translations.literal: When favor and power were present, none dared obstruct discussion; the court ranks looked at one another and changed color; on the roads people covered their eyes and swallowed their voices.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Ya held power none dared object; courtiers blanched and commoners fell silent in fear.

sentences.zh: 今宗社降靈，奸凶盡戮，聖明垂佑，黎庶各安。

translations.literal: Now the altars have descended blessings; traitors and villains are all slaughtered; sagely clarity extends protection; the black-haired people each are secure.
translations.idiomatic: Now the dynasty is blessed, the conspirators dead, and the people at peace.

sentences.zh: 微臣伏蒙天恩，兼授使務，官銜之內，猶帶此名，俯仰若驚，夙宵知愧。

translations.literal: Your humble servant bows to Heaven's grace, also receiving commission duties; within my official title this name still remains—bowing and looking up I am startled; from dawn to night I know shame.
translations.idiomatic: I have received Heaven's grace yet still bear the monopoly title on my commission—an honor that shames me day and night.

sentences.zh: 伏乞特回聖聽，下鑒愚誠，速委宰臣，除此使額。

translations.literal: I bow to beg that Your Majesty especially turn your sacred hearing, look down on my foolish sincerity, quickly entrust chief ministers to remove this commission title.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to hear me and have the chief ministers abolish this commission.

sentences.zh: 緣國家之用或闕，山澤之利有遺，許臣條流，續具奏聞。

translations.literal: Because state use may be short and mountain-and-marsh profits may remain, permit your servant to itemize regulations and continue memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: If revenue is still needed from hills and marshes, I will propose other measures in due course.

sentences.zh: 采造欲及，妨廢為虞。

translations.literal: Harvest and manufacture are about to arrive—I fear obstruction and waste.
translations.idiomatic: The planting season is near—delay will ruin the crop.

sentences.zh: 前月二十一日內殿奏封之次，鄭覃與臣同陳論訖。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of last month, at the inner palace memorial-sealing session, Zheng Tan and your servant together finished stating the discussion.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of last month Zheng Tan and I presented this case in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 伏望聖慈早賜處分，一依舊法，不用新條。

translations.literal: I bow to hope for early imperial grace and disposition—entirely follow the old law, do not use new articles.
translations.idiomatic: I pray for early action: restore the old regulations, not Wang Ya's new rules.

sentences.zh: 惟納榷之時，須節級加價，商人轉抬，必較稍貴，即是錢出萬國，利歸有司，既無害茶商，又不擾茶戶。

translations.literal: Only at the time of accepting monopoly [goods], it is necessary to add price by graded steps; merchants in turning markup must compare slightly dearer—then cash exits the myriad states and profit returns to the offices; thus harming neither tea merchants nor disturbing tea households.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the point of monopoly purchase need prices rise by graded steps; merchants will pass the cost along so revenue flows to the state without harming growers or licensed traders.

sentences.zh: 上以彰陛下愛人之德，下以竭微臣憂國之心。

translations.literal: Above to display Your Majesty's virtue of loving the people; below to exhaust your humble servant's heart of worrying for the state.
translations.idiomatic: This would show Your Majesty's love for the people and fulfill my duty to the realm.

sentences.zh: 遠近傳聞，必當咸悅。

translations.literal: Far and near hearing the report will surely all be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The empire would rejoice.

sentences.zh: 」詔可之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 先是，鹽鐵使王涯表請使茶山之人，移植根本，舊有貯積，皆使焚棄，天下怨之。

translations.literal: Before this, salt-and-iron commissioner Wang Ya had memorialized requesting that tea-mountain people transplant roots; old stores were all ordered burned and discarded—the world resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier salt and iron commissioner Wang Ya had ordered tea mountains uprooted for state plantations and old stocks burned, to universal outrage.

sentences.zh: 及是楚主之，故奏罷焉。

translations.literal: When Chu presided, therefore he memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Chu, now in charge, memorialized to end the policy.

sentences.zh: 開成二年十二月，武甯軍節度使薛元賞奏：「泗口稅場，應是經過衣冠商客金銀、羊馬、斛鬥、見錢、茶鹽、綾絹等，一物已上並稅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Kaicheng, Wuning Military Commissioner Xue Yuanshang memorialized: "The Sizhou tax station—what ought to pass are gentry merchants' gold and silver, sheep and horses, grain, cash, tea, salt, silk, and the like; on every single item tax is levied.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Kaicheng 2 (837) Wuning commissioner Xue Yuanshang reported that Sizhou tax station levied every item passing merchants carried—gold, silver, livestock, grain, cash, tea, salt, silk, and more.

sentences.zh: 今商量，其雜稅並請停絕。

translations.literal: Now on deliberation, the miscellaneous taxes all request cessation.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed abolishing these miscellaneous levies.

sentences.zh: 」詔許之。

translations.literal: " An edict permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 大中六年正月，鹽鐵轉運使裴休奏：「諸道節度、觀察使，置店停上茶商，每斤收搨地錢，並稅經過商人，頗乖法理。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Dazhong, Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Pei Xiu memorialized: "Circuit military commissioners and observation commissioners set shops to detain tea merchants, collect ground-levy cash per jin, and also tax passing merchants—quite contrary to law and principle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dazhong 6 (852) transport commissioner Pei Xiu reported that commissioners were detaining tea merchants, charging ground levies per jin, and taxing travelers—illegal extortion.

sentences.zh: 今請厘革橫稅，以通舟船，商旅既安，課利自厚。

translations.literal: Now I request rectifying and abolishing arbitrary taxes to open passage for boats; when travelers and merchants are secure, tax profits naturally grow thick.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to abolish illegal surcharges so shipping and trade could flourish and lawful revenue would grow.

sentences.zh: 今又正稅茶商，多被私販茶人侵奪其利。

translations.literal: Now again the licensed tea merchants are mostly robbed of their profit by private tea smugglers.
translations.idiomatic: Licensed tea merchants were meanwhile losing out to smugglers.

sentences.zh: 今請強幹官吏，先于出茶山口，及廬、壽、淮南界內，佈置把捉，曉諭招收，量加半稅，給陳首帖子，令其所在公行，從此通流，更無苛奪。

translations.literal: Now I request strong, capable officials first deployed at tea-export mountain passes and within Lu, Shou, and Huainan boundaries to arrange capture, explain and recruit; measure and add half tax, give confession placards, order them to travel openly in each place—from this free circulation, no more harsh seizure.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed posting officers at tea passes and in Lu, Shou, and Huainan to register smugglers at half the regular tax with travel permits, ending arbitrary seizure.

sentences.zh: 所冀招恤窮困，下絕奸欺，使私販者免犯法之憂，正稅者無失利之歎。

translations.literal: The hope is to recruit and comfort the poor, below cut off fraud, making private sellers free of law-breaking worry and licensed taxpayers free of lost-profit sighs.
translations.idiomatic: The goal was to relieve the poor, end extortion, free smugglers from criminal risk, and protect licensed merchants' profits.

sentences.zh: 欲尋究根本，須舉綱條。

translations.literal: Wishing to investigate the root, one must raise the net's main cords.
translations.idiomatic: To fix the root cause required systematic regulations.

sentences.zh: 」敕旨依奏。

translations.literal: An edict followed the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，淮南及天平軍節度使並浙西觀察使，皆奏軍用困竭，伏乞且賜依舊稅茶。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year, Huainan and Tianping military commissioners together with the western Zhe observation commissioner all memorialized that military use was exhausted and begged permission to restore the old tea tax for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: That fourth month Huainan, Tianping, and western Zhe all pleaded military poverty and asked to restore the old tea tax.

sentences.zh: 敕旨：「裴休條流茶法，事極精詳，制置之初，理須畫一。

translations.literal: An edict: "Pei Xiu's itemized tea law is extremely precise and detailed; at the beginning of establishment, principle requires uniformity.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "Pei Xiu's tea regulations are thorough; at inception policy must be uniform.

sentences.zh: 並宜准今年正月二十六日敕處分。

translations.literal: All should follow the disposition of the edict of the twenty-sixth day of the first month of this year.
translations.idiomatic: All circuits shall follow the edict of the twenty-sixth day of this first month.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，初榷酒，天下悉令官釀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong, wine was first monopolized; all under Heaven was ordered to have government brewing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 3 (782) the wine monopoly began: the empire was ordered to brew only under state control.

sentences.zh: 斛收直三千。

translations.literal: Per hu the levy was three thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The levy was three thousand cash per hu.

sentences.zh: 米雖賤，不得減二千。

translations.literal: Even when rice was cheap, it could not be reduced below two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Even when rice was cheap, the levy could not fall below two thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 委州縣綜領。

translations.literal: Administration was entrusted to prefectures and counties for overall management.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties were entrusted with overall administration.

sentences.zh: 醨薄私釀，罪有差。

translations.literal: Private brewing of thin or weak liquor incurred graded penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Private brewing of thin or weak liquor incurred graded penalties.

sentences.zh: 以京師王者都，特免其榷。

translations.literal: Because the capital was the sovereign's seat, the monopoly was specially exempted there.
translations.idiomatic: Because the capital was the sovereign's seat, the monopoly was specially exempted there.

sentences.zh: 元和六年六月，京兆府奏：「榷酒錢除出正酒戶外，一切隨兩稅青苗，據貫均率。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Yuanhe, the Jingzhao government memorialized: "Wine monopoly fees, aside from licensed brewers, should all follow the two-tax and green-sprout levies, apportioned per string."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yuanhe year 6 (811), the Jingzhao government memorialized: "Wine monopoly fees, aside from licensed brewers, should all follow the two-tax and green-sprout levies, apportioned per string."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 會昌六年九月敕：「揚州等八道州府，置榷麹，並置官店沽酒，代百姓納榷酒錢，並充資助軍用，各有榷許限。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Huichang, an edict: "The eight circuits including Yangzhou shall establish yeast monopolies and government wine shops, paying monopoly fees on the people's behalf and applying proceeds to military use, each with set monopoly quotas."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Huichang year 6 (846), an edict: "The eight circuits including Yangzhou shall establish yeast monopolies and government wine shops, paying monopoly fees on the people's behalf for military use, each with set quotas."

sentences.zh: 揚州、陳許、汴州、襄州、河東五處榷麹，浙西、浙東、鄂嶽三處置官沽酒。

translations.literal: Yangzhou, Chenxu, Bian, Xiang, and Hedong—five places—had yeast monopolies; Zhexi, Zhedong, and E-Yue—three places—had government wine sales.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou, Chenxu, Bian, Xiang, and Hedong had yeast monopolies; Zhexi, Zhedong, and E-Yue had government wine sales.

sentences.zh: 如聞禁止私酤，過於嚴酷，一人違犯，連累數家，閭裏之間，不免咨怨。

translations.literal: We hear that prohibiting private sale has been excessively harsh: one person's violation implicates several households, and among neighbors complaints cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that banning private sales has been excessively harsh: one violation implicates several households, and neighbors cannot help but complain.

sentences.zh: 宜從今以後如有人私沽酒及置私麹者，但許罪止一身，並所由容縱，任據罪處分。

translations.literal: Henceforth when anyone privately sells wine or makes private yeast, punishment should be limited to the offender alone; local officers who connive may be punished according to the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth when anyone privately sells wine or makes private yeast, punishment should be limited to the offender alone; local officers who connive may be punished according to the offense.

sentences.zh: 鄉井之內，如不知情，並不得追擾。

translations.literal: Within villages and lanes, those who did not know must not be pursued or harassed.
translations.idiomatic: Within villages and lanes, those who did not know must not be pursued or harassed.

sentences.zh: 其所犯之人，任用重典，兼不得沒入家產。

translations.literal: The offender may be punished by severe statutes, but household property must not be confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The offender may be punished severely, but household property must not be confiscated.
